Emitted for a blocked splunk_run_query (spl = the query; operator = the forbidden command or word, or inline_comment / unbalanced_backtick / unterminated_quote / escaped_quote / external_lookup / fit_into / macro, an allow-list operator or a parser-check operator — see the SPL guard above; command = the refused command, lookup or macro), for a refused saved-search name (spl = (saved search) <name>, operator = saved_search_not_in_catalog) and for an undeclared tool (spl = (tool) <name>, operator = tool_not_declared) rate_limited_prompt (RateLimitedPromptEvent) threshold, countInWindow, promptLength, secondsUntilNextSlot user_prompt_jailbreak_flag (UserPromptJailbreakFlagEvent) promptHash (FNV-1a 32-bit hex), promptLength, matchedGroups: string[], charClassFingerprint: string session_tool_cap_hit (SessionToolCapHitEvent) cap, attemptedCount, toolName daily_spend_cap_hit (DailySpendCapHitEvent) capUsd, spentTodayUsd, promptLength, secondsUntilMidnight audit_forwarder_failure destinationUrl (sanitized — query strings stripped), reason, batchSize forwarder_disabled_acceptance / ai_assistant_enable_acceptance host (Splunk-stamped IP), tcVersion, optInChoice, disclaimerHash model_discovery (ModelDiscoveryEvent) provider, trigger (credential_save / settings_refresh / ttl), ok, modelCount, durationMs, error

All schemas live at components/ai/audit/auditTypes.ts.

docs.title: Splunk reserved-field gotcha
docs.text: The category field on these events is a Splunk reserved name: Splunk’s automatic event classification fills it (with unknown for this sourcetype), and spath does NOT overwrite it. The viewer’s SPL therefore runs | eval category=json_extract(_raw, "category") after spath. It re-derives user the same way, | eval user=json_extract(_raw, "user"): when the base search filters on user, Splunk extracts the field to apply the filter and spath adds the same value again, so without the eval the field has two values and a name shows twice. Replicate both in custom queries.

docs.title: Adding a New Predefined Prompt
docs.text:
The catalog is compiled into the App: the intent map is imported into the bundle, and its saved searches ship in default/savedsearches.conf. A new or changed prompt therefore needs a rebuild of the App from source (Building the Packages from Source) and a redeploy; on Splunk Cloud the rebuilt App goes through private-app vetting again. The steps:

  1. Edit default/data/mcp/logserv_intent_map.json — add a new entry to the prompts array. Required fields: id, pack (sap_basis | security | operations — drives which prompt-browser tab the prompt appears under), savedSearch, label, description, spl, renderHint. Type-optional but present on every shipped prompt (omitting them silently degrades the guidance card, the deep-dive links, and the Dashboard-Focused tab): interpretation, nextSteps, dashboard. Truly optional: chartHint, chartPalette.
  2. Edit default/savedsearches.conf — add a stanza with the same name as the prompt’s savedSearch field. The SPL must match byte-for-byte.
  3. Bump the intent map’s top-level version field.
  4. Run yarn check:intent-map — it also runs automatically as the FIRST step of yarn build / yarn build:templates-only, so drift fails in seconds, before webpack. It asserts byte-equality between each prompt’s spl and its savedsearches.conf stanza, and that every prompt-shaped stanza has a prompt (scheduled rollup jobs are exempt). The sibling gate yarn check:diagnostics runs the other consistency-test suites plus live conf-drift checks and must also pass for any build.
  5. Pre-deploy SPL dry run. Run the new prompt’s SPL in Splunk Web’s Search app against live data (for example over the last 30 days) and confirm the result has rows with the expected fields. Field-extraction problems often show only against live data.
  6. Bump UI App [install] build in app.conf to bust Splunk Web’s static-asset cache, then build and deploy the App.

docs.title: Intent map JSON schema
docs.text:
interface IntentMapPrompt {
    id: string;
    pack: 'sap_basis' | 'security' | 'operations';
    savedSearch: string;
    label: string;
    description: string;
    spl: string;
    renderHint: 'table' | 'timechart' | 'kpi' | 'pie';
    chartHint?: 'timechart' | 'kpi' | 'pie';
    chartPalette?: 'volume' | 'errors' | 'errors-2' | 'errors-3' | 'auth' | 'status' | 'categorical' | 'neutral';
    dashboard?: string | string[];
    interpretation?: string;
    nextSteps?: Array<string | { text: string; savedSearch?: string; spl?: string }>;
}

docs.title: Splunk risky-command safeguard
docs.text:
Splunk Web’s Search app asks for confirmation before it runs a search that arrives in a link (a URL to /app/search/search?q=..., which is what the ↗ Run SPL chips open) and contains a command Splunk marks as risky. Splunk’s SPL-safeguards documentation for 9.4 lists collect, delete, dump, map, mcollect, meventcollect, outputcsv, outputlookup, run, runshellscript, script, sendalert, sendemail and tscollect. An app can mark further commands with is_risky = true in its commands.conf; the comments in utils/splGuard.ts record that the search app does this for createrss. The list can differ in another Splunk version and grow with the apps installed, so check it on the version you ship to.

Scan all SPL — including nextSteps.spl deep-dive strings — for these commands before shipping. Every command named above is also in FORBIDDEN_SPL_COMMANDS in utils/splGuard.ts, so a scan against that list covers them. Rewrite map-style cross-row dispatches to first-class subsearch syntax: [ search ... | top 1 X | fields X ].

docs.title: Adding a New Audit Event Category
docs.text:
1. Edit components/ai/audit/auditTypes.ts — add a new TypeScript interface extending AuditEventBase with the category-specific fields. Add the type to the AuditEvent union.
  2. Add the new category id to the discriminator string-literal type.
  3. Find the call site that should emit the event. Construct the event object and call ctx.actions.recordAudit(event).
  4. Edit utils/auditQuery.ts — add the category id to AUDIT_CATEGORIES (keep it alphabetical; this drives the viewer’s filter chips and the category union).
  5. Edit components/AuditLogViewer.tsx — add a case to renderHighlight so the row shows its most actionable fields. Do NOT append to CATEGORY_ACCENT_ORDER unless ACCENT_PALETTE grows in lockstep — it maps positionally onto the 11-colour palette; an unlisted category deliberately falls back to the dormant grey via chipColorForCategory.
  6. Bump the UI App build.

The audit writer (components/ai/audit/auditWriter.ts) sends events to BOTH the local logserv_ai_assistant_audit index AND the optional HEC forwarder. No code change needed at the writer layer for new categories.

docs.title: System Primer Architecture
docs.text:
Two primer variants ship: SYSTEM_PRIMER_TIER1 and SYSTEM_PRIMER_TIER2. Both live in hooks/useAIAssistant.ts as module-private constants (only SAVED_SEARCH_DASHBOARDS and the hook itself are exported — a consumer needing primer text must export it first). They share most of their content; the differences:

  • Tier 1 primer instructs the AI that summaries it receives are count + execution-time only, and to write SHAPE-aware narrative (“X rows returned for the search’s rolling window”) rather than inventing concrete values.
  • Tier 2 primer informs the AI that summaries include aggregated metadata (per-column cardinality, top-N values + counts, numeric stats, time range), and instructs it to ground every claim in the actual values from the aggregates. Its TIER 2 SUMMARY SHAPES block explains col_N and the withheld-names line, <redacted-…> tags, values withheld, not in row form and Time range: not shown, and tells the model never to guess, recover or attribute a withheld name or a redacted value and to name an identifier only when it appears in clear; synthesis rule 3 grounds claims in values shown in clear.

Both primers include:

  • The TOOL_RESULT_DATA boundary block (<TOOL_RESULT_DATA>...</TOOL_RESULT_DATA> sentinels)
  • The TIME-WINDOW REASONING block
  • The canonical saved-search catalog
  • The LogServ data model (sourcetypes + key fields, for ad-hoc SPL)
  • The decision rule for splunk_run_saved_search vs splunk_run_query
  • The SYNTHESIS RULES section: lettered finding format, severity-dot rendering, citation format, etc.

Power Mode augmentation: when the user has Power Mode on, POWER_MODE_RULE_SUFFIX is appended to the primer at dispatch time via unwrapVisible(content) + suffix then markVisible() (the brand type can’t widen back automatically).

docs.title: Pre-Resolving Drill-Down URLs at the Orchestrator Layer
docs.text:
The drill-down chip URLs (↗ Dashboard, ↗ Run SPL) are pre-resolved at the AIAssistant.tsx layer, where each tool result’s exact dispatch window is known. The resolved URLs are stored on the citationLookup Map for the chat parser to consume:

const citationLookup: Map<string, { toolUseId: string; splUrl?: string }> = new Map();
toolResultsInOrder.forEach((tr) => {
    if (tr.displayName) {
        const splUrl = tr.spl
            ? buildSplunkSearchUrl(tr.spl, tr.earliest, tr.latest)
            : undefined;
        citationLookup.set(tr.displayName, { toolUseId: tr.toolUseId, splUrl });
    }
});

The chat-side renderer (ChatMessage.tsx) is dumb — it just renders <a href={entry.splUrl}> when the lookup carries a URL. This avoids duplicating SPL-lookup logic at every consumer.

Same pattern applies to the dashboard chips: the dashboardLinks are resolved once via resolveDashboardLinks(slugs) at the orchestrator and consumed as {slug, name, url} triples.

docs.title: Legal Acknowledgement Modal Trigger Logic
docs.text:
Two legal acknowledgement modals gate Settings save flows:

  • Enable Acceptance Modal — gates enabled = true saves.
  • Forwarder Disabled Acceptance Modal — gates audit_forwarder_enabled = false saves.

Both follow Splunk’s splunk_instrumentation optInVersion framework with one extension. The trigger logic is:

isEnableTcPending = (
    (saved.enabled === false && draft.enabled === true)  // deliberate toggle-on
    OR
    (currentOptInVersion > acknowledgedVersion)          // version bumped
)

The pure optInVersion-only path is what Splunk’s stock telemetry uses (acknowledge once per version, durable until bump). We added the deliberate-toggle-transition trigger because re-enabling AI Assistant after a disable is a deliberate user action that warrants re-acknowledgement of the legal posture each time. The acknowledged version is stored once per deployment (KV Store collection logserv_ai_assistant_acks, _key = the stanza name), not per user, and a Yes and a No both record it.

  • A No on the enable re-ask (the AI Assistant already on) turns the AI Assistant off: it first writes enabled = false - the rest of the draft is not applied - and then records the No, so a failed write leaves the question pending. The turn-off writes the page’s settings whole, like every Save: a partial write would merge onto readAIConfig(), which falls back to the conf or the defaults when the KV read fails. The page stays busy until the No is recorded, and the No’s audit event records the saved provider.
  • Closing. The dialog closes before the page state changes, and an answer that cannot be recorded also closes the dialog, so its error is seen. The forwarder dialog likewise closes before a record or save error is shown.
  • Audit events. handleForwarderChoice posts the forwarder acknowledgement’s audit event as soon as the answer is recorded, before the save a Yes goes on to. AuditWriter.postOneOff reads the local index and the forwarder settings before its first await, so the settings in place when a one-off event is posted decide where it goes, and a failed forward’s record goes to the event’s index.
  • Provider names. On a re-ask the enablement dialog names saved.provider; when the same save changes the provider, the dialog also gets pendingProviderName.

telemetryConfApi.ts exposes readTcAcknowledgement(stanza) / writeTcAcknowledgement(stanza, choice, version) parameterized by stanza name. The two modal stanzas are constants: STANZA_FORWARDER_TC and STANZA_ENABLE_TC.

The legacy conf-writer path coerces yes/no to '1'/'0'; the KV Store path stores the strings as-is. The audit event preserves the literal string in _raw, so the audit event is the canonical record while the stored acknowledgement is the state marker.

docs.title: Why Primer Rules Beat Other Fixes (TIME-WINDOW REASONING)
docs.text:
One alternative fix was considered before settling on primer rules for the time-window reasoning behavior: surfacing the dispatch window in Tier 2 metadata even for non-_time results, which would let the AI see the window directly without reasoning about it. Higher engineering effort than primer rules; deferred unless rules alone don’t move the needle.

Primer rules were the cheapest test of “is this a primer-rules issue?” and it worked: same prompt, same data, dramatically better self-correction behavior in one turn instead of needing a follow-up prompt to re-rank cumulative-noise findings.

This is the canonical pattern: when the AI has the data but isn’t using it correctly, primer rules are the cheapest first attempt. When the AI doesn’t have the data, metadata expansion is the next step.

docs.title: Splunk Static-Asset Cache Busting
docs.text:
Splunk Web caches the React bundle’s asset URL under a hash that includes the [install] build integer in app.conf (src/main/resources/splunk/default/app.conf). Re-deploying the same build number with new bytes serves stale assets even after Splunkd restart. Always bump the build number for any meaningful code change. webpack also reads the version and build from that file at compile time for the About dialog.

The 3-part SemVer in [id] version (and [launcher] version) is independent of the build number and changes only on user-facing version bumps. AppInspect requires a 3-part SemVer version there.

docs.title: Live UI Refresh on Settings Save
docs.text:
When the admin saves a config change in the General tab that affects what users see (master enabled toggle, mcp_required, power_user_roles, etc.), the React app re-runs loadAIAssistantConfig() immediately and re-applies the new config to the running session. No page reload required.

Implementation: App.tsx passes a callback (refreshAIConfig) that re-reads the config with loadAIAssistantConfig(), which goes through readAIConfig(): the KV Store collection logserv_ai_assistant_settings first, then the conf, then the defaults (writeAIConfig clears the read cache, so the read sees the new values). The callback is threaded App → AppShell (onAIConfigSaved) → AIAssistantSettings (onConfigSaved) → GeneralPanel, called after writeAIConfig succeeds. Affected props are recomputed on the next React render and the dependent UI re-renders accordingly (e.g., the AI Assistant button in the header appears / disappears).

docs.title: Building the Packages from Source
docs.text:
This page shows how to build each package of Splunk for SAP LogServ from the repository’s sources and how to vet a build with AppInspect. Use it when you need a variant that is not published, such as the templates-only LogServ App, or when you change the source. For a normal install, use the tarballs in the repository’s release_binaries/.

Paths are relative to the repository root; the sources are under sap_logserv_package/.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
Package Source Tools Output LogServ App (splunk_app_sap_logserv) sap_logserv_package/splunk_app_sap_logserv/, a Yarn workspace; the App is packages/log-serv-app Node.js 22 or later, Yarn 1.x (Classic), GNU tar packages/log-serv-app/stage/, then a tarball you create Data TA (splunk_ta_sap_logserv) sap_logserv_package/splunk_ta_sap_logserv/ A Python 3 virtual environment with UCC (splunk-add-on-ucc-framework) 6.6.0 output/splunk_ta_sap_logserv/ and splunk_ta_sap_logserv-<version>.tar.gz LogServ Azure add-on (splunk_ta_sap_logserv_azure) sap_logserv_package/splunk_ta_sap_logserv_azure/ The same UCC environment splunk_ta_sap_logserv_azure-<version>.tar.gz LogServ GCP add-on (splunk_ta_sap_logserv_gcp) sap_logserv_package/splunk_ta_sap_logserv_gcp/ The same UCC environment splunk_ta_sap_logserv_gcp-<version>.tar.gz

The 0.1.2 release was built with Node.js 23 and Yarn 1.22 for the App, UCC 6.6.0 for the three add-ons, and AppInspect 4.3.1. Both builds download packages (from the npm registry and from PyPI), so they need network access.

Versions are 3-part SemVer (for example 0.1.2): AppInspect rejects a 4-part version.

docs.title: Build the LogServ App
docs.text:
1. Install the dependencies at the workspace root:

    cd sap_logserv_package/splunk_app_sap_logserv
yarn install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-engines

    --frozen-lockfile installs exactly what yarn.lock records and fails instead of changing it. --ignore-engines is needed on Node.js 23, because a development dependency (jest 30) declares an engines range that leaves Node.js 23 out.

  2. If you changed the source, set the version and the build number in packages/log-serv-app/src/main/resources/splunk/default/app.conf: [id] version and [launcher] version for a new version (and version in src/main/resources/splunk/app.manifest), and a higher [install] build for every change. Splunk Web caches the App’s assets by build number, so a new build with an unchanged number serves stale files; see Splunk Static-Asset Cache Busting.

  3. Build:

    cd packages/log-serv-app
yarn build

    yarn build runs these steps in order and stops at the first that fails:

    • bin/check-intent-map.js: each predefined prompt’s SPL must equal its savedsearches.conf stanza byte for byte, and every prompt-shaped stanza must have a prompt
    • bin/check-diagnostics.js: the consistency-test suites and the conf-drift checks
    • bin/build.js build: the production webpack build into stage/ (it empties stage/ first)
    • yarn types:build (tsc): type-checks the source and writes declaration files to types/
    • bin/generate-sbom.js: stage/SBOM.json
    • bin/generate-third-party-notices.js: stage/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, generated from the installed node_modules/

    yarn build:ci runs yarn audit --groups dependencies --level high first and fails on a high or critical advisory.

  4. Package stage/ with the App’s directory name at the top, in the same directory:

    tar -czf splunk_app_sap_logserv-0.1.2.tar.gz --transform 's|^stage|splunk_app_sap_logserv|' stage

    --transform is a GNU tar option (Linux, and Git Bash on Windows).

For local development, yarn link:app links stage/ into $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/splunk_app_sap_logserv (bin/build.js link).

Do not use build_logserv_app.sh

sap_logserv_package/build_logserv_app.sh predates the React App: it copies splunk_app_sap_logserv/package/, a directory that no longer exists. Build the App with Yarn as above.

docs.title: The Templates-Only Variant
docs.text:
cd sap_logserv_package/splunk_app_sap_logserv/packages/log-serv-app
yarn build:templates-only

This runs the same steps with the compile-time TEMPLATES_ONLY flag: bin/build.js build --templates-only sets LOGSERV_TEMPLATES_ONLY=true for webpack. The resulting bundle reports the runtime templates_only_mode setting as on at every config read, whatever is stored, and hides that toggle. After webpack, the build sets templates_only_mode = true in the staged stage/default/ai_assistant_settings.conf (the source file is not changed) and fails if it cannot verify the change. The vendor provider code stays in the bundle, unreachable. Package stage/ as in step 4. yarn build:ci:templates-only adds the audit gate.

What the variant does and does not restrict is described in Restricting the LLM Path and The Build Flag Pattern.

docs.title: Build the Data TA
docs.text:
The Data TA, the LogServ Azure add-on and the LogServ GCP add-on are UCC add-ons. ucc-gen build generates the add-on from globalConfig.json and package/, installs the Python packages listed in package/lib/requirements.txt into its lib/, and then runs the add-on’s additional_packaging.py; ucc-gen package makes the tarball. What additional_packaging.py patches is described in Data TA Internals.

  1. Create a Python virtual environment with UCC (once):

    python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install splunk-add-on-ucc-framework==6.6.0

  2. If you changed the source, set the version in meta.version of splunk_ta_sap_logserv/globalConfig.json, and keep version in package/app.manifest the same.

  3. With the virtual environment active, build from sap_logserv_package/:

    cd sap_logserv_package
bash build_logserv_ta.sh 0.1.2

    Run the wrappers with bash: they are committed without the executable bit, so ./build_logserv_ta.sh fails with “Permission denied” in a fresh clone.

    The wrapper first deletes every splunk_ta_sap_logserv-*.tar.gz and the output/splunk_ta_sap_logserv/ directory in the current directory (move a tarball you want to keep out of it first), then runs:

    ucc-gen build --source splunk_ta_sap_logserv/package --ta-version 0.1.2
ucc-gen package --path output/splunk_ta_sap_logserv

  4. Check the build output for this line, and for any WARNING:

    [additional_packaging] Patched metadata/default.meta: added sc_subadmin to global write ACL.

requirements.txt pins every package to an exact version with its sha256 hashes, so pip refuses a downloaded file that does not match. The add-on sources have no default/app.conf: UCC generates it, writes the version into it and stamps [install] build with the time of the build in Unix seconds. That is why add-on builds have numbers such as 1792598960 (2026-10-21 16:09:20 UTC). Every 0.1.2 build has the same [launcher] version, which matters when a Deployment Server distributes the Data TA; see Deployment-Apps Sync.

docs.title: Build the LogServ Azure and GCP Add-ons
docs.text:
Use the same virtual environment. Set the version in each add-on’s globalConfig.json (meta.version) and package/app.manifest, then build from sap_logserv_package/:

cd sap_logserv_package
bash build_logserv_azure_ta.sh 0.1.2
bash build_logserv_gcp_ta.sh 0.1.2

Each wrapper deletes its own old tarball and output/ directory, then runs ucc-gen build --source splunk_ta_sap_logserv_azure/package --ta-version <version> and ucc-gen package --path output/splunk_ta_sap_logserv_azure (for GCP, splunk_ta_sap_logserv_gcp). Check the output for these lines (Azure shown; for GCP they name sap_logserv_gcp_pubsub and cloud_provider::gcp):

[additional_packaging] Overwrote UCC stub with real bin/sap_logserv_azure_queue.py.
[additional_packaging] Patched inputs.conf: [sap_logserv_azure_queue] python.required + _meta = cloud_provider::azure.
[additional_packaging] Patched metadata/default.meta: added sc_subadmin to global write ACL.

The wrappers’ closing hint still names an older input file (azure_queue_input.py, gcp_queue_input.py); go by the lines above.

docs.title: Vet a Package with AppInspect
docs.text:
Run Splunk AppInspect on every tarball before you install or publish it, always with --included-tags cloud, which adds the Splunk Cloud vetting checks:

pip install splunk-appinspect==4.3.1
splunk-appinspect inspect splunk_ta_sap_logserv-0.1.2.tar.gz \
    --mode precert --included-tags cloud \
    --output-file appinspect_cloud_logserv_ta.json --data-format json
  • The target is 0 errors, 0 failures and 0 future failures.
  • Compare each check with the published report of the canonical build in release_binaries/ (appinspect_cloud_logserv_app-0.1.2.json, appinspect_cloud_logserv_ta-0.1.2.json, appinspect_cloud_logserv_azure_ta-0.1.2.json, appinspect_cloud_logserv_gcp_ta-0.1.2.json). A check whose result changed needs a reason.
  • Treat a check_for_existence_of_python_code_block_in_mako_template warning as a blocker: AppInspect reports it only as a warning, but Splunk Cloud Victoria enforces the rule when the page is served, and the page then fails to load.

The run_appinspect.sh script in the Data TA source runs without --included-tags cloud; use the command above instead.

docs.title: Data TA Internals
docs.text: This page describes how the Data TA (splunk_ta_sap_logserv) works inside: its filtering, its Deployment Server automation, the server-side part of the AWS S3 Direct screen, its build-time patches, and the internals of the LogServ Azure and GCP add-ons. It is for developers who maintain, extend or test these packages; to install or configure them, use the install guides.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The filtering system provides index-time event filtering via TRANSFORMS-based queue routing. It includes a UI built on UCC (Splunk Universal Configuration Console), custom REST handlers, Deployment Server automation, and background scripted inputs for daily maintenance and upgrade detection.

docs.title: Build-Time Patches
docs.text:
additional_packaging.py runs after ucc-gen build has generated the add-on (UCC calls its cleanup_output_files()) and patches the output in seven steps:

  1. Points the generated settings handler (bin/splunk_ta_sap_logserv_rh_settings.py) at FilterSettingsHandler instead of the stock AdminExternalHandler. UCC wires custom handlers only for tabs with a table, and the Filters tab is a settings tab.
  2. Adds handlertype, python.version, python.required = 3.13 and passSystemAuth = true to every [admin_external:*] stanza of restmap.conf. python.required clears an AppInspect future failure. Splunk defines passSystemAuth only for [script:*] stanzas, so on [admin_external:*] it has no effect: the settings saves of sc_subadmin and other roles without admin_all_objects are carried by the handler’s filesystem fallback (step 2 of Configuration REST Handler). The comment in additional_packaging.py that says otherwise is out of date.
  3. Appends the [script:] stanzas of the two persistent endpoints, deployment_push and s3_direct_meta, to restmap.conf.
  4. Appends their [expose:] stanzas to web.conf (see web.conf Expose Stanza).
  5. Removes gRPC, protobuf and OpenTelemetry packages from lib/ if a dependency ever brings them in: their binaries fail AppInspect’s AArch64 check. The solnlib pin below 8 in lib/requirements.txt keeps them out in the first place.
  6. Adds python.required = 3.13 to the [script://...] stanzas of inputs.conf.
  7. Adds sc_subadmin to the global write ACL in metadata/default.meta (below).

Several of these are AppInspect Cloud fixes: deleting or truncating the file silently regresses the AppInspect result and locks out a delegated sc_subadmin role. How to run the build is described in Building the Packages from Source.

docs.title: The sc_subadmin Write-ACL Patch
docs.text:
UCC’s build template writes write : [ admin, sc_admin ] into the generated metadata/default.meta and ignores the value in the source’s package/metadata/default.meta, so it grants write only to admin and sc_admin. Some Splunk Cloud stacks give their administrators a delegated-admin role named sc_subadmin. Splunk does not supply this role, and the packages grant it write access by name (see Splunk Cloud roles). Without the patch, that role gets 403 on every write to an object the Data TA owns. (The docstring of additional_packaging.py that calls sc_subadmin the customer’s top administrator role is out of date.) Step 7 re-adds it after the UCC step, and the build prints:

[additional_packaging] Patched metadata/default.meta: added sc_subadmin to global write ACL.

The LogServ Azure and GCP add-ons apply the same patch in their own additional_packaging.py.

To patch a Data TA that is already built, without running UCC again, use the standalone repair script tools/scripts/patch_data_ta_sc_subadmin_metadata.py:

# Against an extracted Data TA directory:
python3 tools/scripts/patch_data_ta_sc_subadmin_metadata.py /path/to/extracted/splunk_ta_sap_logserv

# Against a tarball (extracts, patches, repacks in place + .pre-sc_subadmin-patch.bak backup):
python3 tools/scripts/patch_data_ta_sc_subadmin_metadata.py --tarball /path/to/splunk_ta_sap_logserv-X.Y.Z.tar.gz

Both invocations are idempotent: running on already-patched input is a no-op (a tarball is then neither repacked nor backed up). The script exits 0 when it patched or found nothing to change; 1 when the tarball or metadata/default.meta is missing, or the file does not hold the expected stock ACL; and 2 when a tar step fails or the tarball does not hold exactly one top-level directory. A failed repack restores the tarball from the backup.

docs.title: Core Library
docs.text:
splunk_ta_sap_logserv_filter_utils.py

This is the central module. All other components import from it.

docs.title: Key Functions
docs.text: Function Purpose get_app_path() Determines the app installation path (checks SPLUNK_HOME, falls back to relative path) discover_supported_types(app_path) Scans default/transforms.conf for @logserv_filter annotations find_uncovered_types(supported, patterns) Compares supported types against user include patterns parse_comma_patterns(string) Splits a folder-pattern field (Include / Exclude Filters) into a list; empty entries are dropped parse_source_patterns(value) Splits a source field (Include / Exclude Sources) into its entries; only spaces around an entry are stripped, and empty entries are kept so that validation rejects a doubled or trailing comma validate_patterns(patterns, field_name) Validates folder-pattern syntax (dir/subdir format, valid characters) validate_single_pattern(pattern) Validates one folder pattern against rules validate_source_entry(entry) / validate_source_patterns(patterns, field_name) Validate source entries against the grammar in Validation Layers; the message names the field and the entry validate_source_field(value, field_name) Validates a whole source field value as submitted or stored: its length, then every entry filter_pattern_fragment(pattern) The hand-written translator f(p): one folder segment or source pattern to the REGEX fragment of a JSON value; raises on any character it does not know filter_lookahead(key, fragment) One condition LA(key, frag) for clz_dir, clz_subdir or source is_pass_all_include(include_patterns) Whether Include Filters keeps every event (no include gate) fnmatch_patterns_to_combined_regex(patterns) Compatibility helper kept for existing importers: one REGEX in the generator’s shape for a folder list, without chunking epoch_cutoff_from_days(days_in_past) Computes the epoch timestamp for midnight N days ago (UTC) generate_epoch_less_than_regex(cutoff_epoch) Generates a digit-by-digit regex matching epoch values less than the cutoff generate_transforms_stanzas(include, exclude, days, include_sources=None, exclude_sources=None) Generates the filter transform stanzas; re-validates every entry and raises on an invalid one generate_props_filter_lines(include, exclude, days, enabled, include_sources=None, exclude_sources=None) Generates the TRANSFORMS-00-filter line naming exactly the stanzas generate_transforms_stanzas emits, in chain order write_local_conf(app_path, conf_name, content) Writes between marker comments in local conf files write_local_conf_section(app_path, conf_name, content, marker_start, marker_end) Generalised marker-block writer — lets two independent marker blocks (filter + cloud provider) coexist in one local conf update_local_stanza(app_path, conf_name, stanza, kv) Direct filesystem stanza write — the RestError[403] fallback used when the caller lacks admin_all_objects get_ta_version(app_path) Reads [launcher] version from default/app.conf (falls back to app.manifest if not present) get_server_roles(session_key) Queries /services/server/info for roles is_deployment_server(session_key) Two-step DS detection (roles + client probe) get_deployment_apps_path() Returns the etc/deployment-apps/ path for the TA ensure_deployment_app_synced(app_path) Copies the full app to deployment-apps/ when no copy exists or the [launcher] version differs; otherwise does nothing (see Deployment-Apps Sync) mirror_to_deployment_apps(app_path) Copies local/transforms.conf and local/props.conf ensure_serverclass(session_key) Creates server class + app mapping via REST + file

docs.title: Constants
docs.text: Constant Value Purpose APP_NAME splunk_ta_sap_logserv App directory name SERVERCLASS_NAME SAP_LogServ_HeavyForwarders Auto-created server class name SETTINGS_CONF splunk_ta_sap_logserv_settings UCC settings conf file FILTER_STANZA filter_settings Stanza name in settings conf SYSTEM_MESSAGE_NAME logserv_filter_upgrade_warning System message banner name for upgrade warnings ANNOTATION_PATTERN Compiled regex Matches @logserv_filter: annotation comment lines VALID_SEGMENT_PATTERN Compiled regex Validates characters in dir/subdir pattern segments FILTER_REGEX_SKIP Regex text (SKIP in Filter Regex Generation) Where every generated filter REGEX starts: the line start, or just past the _raw value FILTER_REGEX_GAP Regex text (the gap inside LA in Filter Regex Generation) What a lookahead may cross before its key: anything on the line except a "_raw" key FILTER_LOOKAHEAD 100000 LOOKAHEAD of every generated filter stanza (= TRUNCATE in default/props.conf) FILTER_REGEX_MAX_CHARS 8000 A list whose REGEX would pass this many characters is split into numbered stanzas SOURCE_PATTERN_MAX_LEN / SOURCE_FIELD_MAX_LEN 512 / 4096 Longest source pattern / longest source field value FILTER_MARKER_START / FILTER_MARKER_END Marker comments Delimit generated filter content in local conf files CLOUD_PROVIDER_MARKER_START / CLOUD_PROVIDER_MARKER_END Marker comments Delimit the generated [logserv_set_cloud_provider] block — separate from the filter block so the daily time-refresh preserves it

docs.title: Configuration REST Handler (Filters + Cloud Provider tabs)
docs.text:
splunk_ta_sap_logserv_rh_filter_settings.py

UCC REST handler (extends AdminExternalHandler) registered in globalConfig.json. UCC generates ONE MultipleModel settings endpoint shared by all Configuration tabs, so this single handler class serves both the Filters and the Cloud Provider tab — it dispatches on the payload (if 'cloud_provider' in self.callerArgs.data), validating against VALID_CLOUD_PROVIDERS and writing/clearing the [logserv_set_cloud_provider] override inside its own CLOUD_PROVIDER marker block (see Marker Comments); on a DS it then syncs, mirrors and reloads as a Filters save does. For a Filters save it handles the Save action:

  1. Validates patterns server-side (blocks save on failure via admin.ArgValidationException): include_sources and exclude_sources on every save, then every posted value on every save for conf safety (_validate_posted_values(): no control character, tab included, and no trailing backslash), the folder patterns and Days in the Past when filtering is enabled — see Validation Layers
  2. Saves settings to splunk_ta_sap_logserv_settings.conf (default UCC behavior — the happy path). Falls back to a direct filesystem write when the UCC REST write raises RestError[403] (“This operation is forbidden”): splunkd gates /configs/conf-* writes on admin_all_objects independently of the object metadata ACL, so Splunk Cloud sc_subadmin and hardened on-prem admin roles fail the REST path. update_local_stanza() writes the stanza to local/<settings>.conf directly, bypassing that gate (passSystemAuth is NOT honoured for UCC [admin_external:*] handlers)
  3. Generates local/transforms.conf and local/props.conf with filter stanzas, from all five filter fields (include_filters, exclude_filters, include_sources, exclude_sources, days_in_past) as saved: _effective_filter_settings() takes each field the request posts (an emptied field is '', as splunktaucclib stores it), and for a field a partial REST/CLI save leaves out the stored value (one GET of configs/conf-splunk_ta_sap_logserv_settings/filter_settings, only when a field is missing; on a read failure the old defaults, with a WARNING). Step 1 dry-runs the generators on these values when filtering is enabled, so a value they would refuse is refused before anything is saved
  4. Syncs and mirrors to deployment-apps if on a DS (full app copy only on the first copy or a version change, then the filter configs; see Deployment-Apps Sync)
  5. Creates server class if on a DS (first time only)
  6. Reloads confs via REST API (/servicesNS/nobody/splunk_ta_sap_logserv/configs/conf-transforms/_reload and .../conf-props/_reload, then /services/data/transforms/extractions/_reload and /services/data/props/extractions/_reload)
  7. Checks for uncovered types and manages system message banner

docs.title: Deploy Button REST Handler
docs.text:
splunk_ta_sap_logserv_rh_deployment_push.py

Persistent REST handler (PersistentServerConnectionApplication) registered in restmap.conf and gated by the edit_deployment_server capability. Provides two endpoints:

  • GET /services/splunk_ta_sap_logserv/deployment_push — Returns is_deployment_server and, on a DS, the status of the SAP_LogServ_HeavyForwarders server class (exists, disabled, has client targeting); the JS hooks use it to render the UI
  • POST — Triggers a Deployment Server reload via /services/deployment/server/config/_reload

Deploy to Forwarders reloads the whole Deployment Server. /services/deployment/server/config/_reload reloads every server class on the DS, not only SAP_LogServ_HeavyForwarders, so pending changes in other server classes are pushed at the same time. The Daily Time Refresh uses the scoped serverclasses/<name>/reload instead.

As a persistent handler it sets up its own sys.path and needs an [expose:] stanza; see Persistent Handler sys.path and web.conf Expose Stanza.

docs.title: AWS S3 Direct Stamp Handler
docs.text:
splunk_ta_sap_logserv_rh_s3_direct_meta.py

Persistent REST handler behind POST /services/splunk_ta_sap_logserv/s3_direct_meta (form field name). The AWS S3 Direct screen (appserver/static/logserv_s3_direct.js) creates Generic S3 inputs (aws_s3://) in the Splunk Add-on for AWS through that add-on’s own UCC endpoint, which has no _meta field. Right after each create succeeds, the screen calls this handler, which:

  1. accepts only the input names the screen generates (logserv_backfill_<job>_<folder-slug>_<year>);
  2. writes _meta = cloud_provider::aws into that input’s stanza through /servicesNS/nobody/Splunk_TA_aws/configs/conf-inputs/;
  3. disables and re-enables that one input through data/inputs/aws_s3/<name>, so the input starts again from the stanza as written.

It calls splunkd with the caller’s session token and has no passSystemAuth or capability line, so every write is checked against the caller’s own permissions. The screen therefore offers its Create button only to a user with admin_all_objects; for anyone else it shows the generated configuration for an administrator to apply. The handler stamps every input it creates without looking at the Cloud Provider dropdown, so with the dropdown on AWS both stamps are written; see Choose Cloud Attribution.

docs.title: UCC Hooks
docs.text:
filter_settings_hook.js

JavaScript hook loaded by UCC on the Filters tab. cloud_provider_hook.js does the same on the Cloud Provider tab, with its own Deploy to Forwarders button. Lifecycle methods:

  • onCreate / onRender / onEditLoad — Calls checkDeploymentServer() to GET the deployment push endpoint. If DS detected, injects the deploy banner, server class guidance notices, and Deploy button into the DOM
  • onSaveSuccess — Triggers window.location.reload() after 500ms to reflect server-side changes

docs.title: Daily Time Refresh
docs.text:
logserv_filter_time_refresh.py

Scripted input (runs every 86400 seconds / once per day):

  1. Reads filter settings from the settings conf via REST — all six keys: filter_enabled, include_filters, exclude_filters, include_sources, exclude_sources, days_in_past
  2. Regenerates local/transforms.conf and local/props.conf with updated epoch cutoff regex
  3. Mirrors to deployment-apps if on a DS
  4. Reloads the SAP_LogServ_HeavyForwarders server class if on a DS, in the namespace of the app that holds it (see below), so the heavy forwarders fetch the new cutoff on their next phone-home
  5. Reloads confs

It does steps 2–5 only while filtering is enabled and days_in_past is above 0; otherwise it logs why and exits.

Where the scoped reload is sent. A server-class reload (deployment/server/serverclasses/<name>/reload) has to be sent in the namespace of the app whose serverclass.conf holds the class. ensure_serverclass() creates the class through /services/... as the admin who saves the filters, so it lands in that admin’s default app — typically search, where its ACL reads app = search, owner = nobody, sharing = app. A POST to /services/deployment/server/serverclasses/SAP_LogServ_HeavyForwarders/reload resolves in the default app of splunk-system-user (the input’s passAuth user), which need not be the app that holds the class, so the refresh resolves the namespace instead:

  1. GET /servicesNS/-/-/deployment/server/serverclasses/SAP_LogServ_HeavyForwarders?output_mode=json (read-only) and take entry[0].acl.app; the value is used only if it is a plain app name — it matches [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+ and is not dots only — because it becomes part of a URL path
  2. POST /servicesNS/nobody/<app>/deployment/server/serverclasses/SAP_LogServ_HeavyForwarders/reload
  3. On any failure — no owning app, a refused or failed POST — fall back to /servicesNS/nobody/search/..., then to /services/...; a path already tried is not tried again, and the first HTTP 200 or 201 ends the sequence

It logs at INFO which path reloaded the class, or a WARNING that lists every path tried and its result when none did. No reload failure raises out of main(), and the conf reload of step 5 runs either way. A failed reload only delays the forwarders: they keep the previous cutoff until the next Deploy to Forwarders, and a stale cutoff is less restrictive — older events pass — never more.

A working reload restarts the forwarders once a day. The cutoff text changes every UTC day, so each run gives the forwarders a changed app, and ensure_serverclass() maps the Data TA with restartSplunkd = true — each heavy forwarder in the class restarts to apply it. The refresh runs every 86,400 seconds counted from the Deployment Server’s last start, so that restart is not tied to a maintenance window. Only a Deployment Server with filtering enabled and days_in_past above 0 does this.

It must read every filter field. The refresh rewrites the whole FILTER marker block, so a field it does not read and pass to the generators disappears from the generated rules within a day — and on a DS the stripped block is mirrored and pushed to the heavy forwarders by the scoped reload. Any new filter field must be threaded through this script as well as the REST handler.

Invalid stored values: the generators re-validate every entry and raise on an invalid one (for example a hand-edited local/splunk_ta_sap_logserv_settings.conf). The refresh generates both files before writing either; on an error it logs an ERROR (level=ERROR in the script’s stderr, which splunkd logs under component=ExecProcessor), writes and mirrors nothing, and leaves the last good block in local/transforms.conf and local/props.conf in place. It never emits a REGEX built from unvalidated text. A stored Include Sources while Include Filters is pass-all is not an error here: the refresh ignores it and logs a WARNING (the handler refuses that combination at save time when filtering is enabled).

days_in_past takes the same ERROR path. get_filter_settings() parses it with parse_days_in_past(), the parser the generators use at save, so every value a save turned into a time filter (7, 7.0, 1e1) is refreshed too; None / '' read as 0 (no time filter, no refresh). A stored value that is not a finite whole number comes back as days_error, and main() logs it at ERROR through log_not_refreshed() — the same message as an invalid pattern — and writes nothing, so the last good block stays in place. A value whose cutoff would fall before 1970 is refused by the generators the same way.

Deployment client guard: on a deployment client whose Data TA came from the DS, the script skips the refresh, so a heavy forwarder never overwrites the filter configs the DS pushed; see Deployment Client Guard.

docs.title: Upgrade Coverage Check
docs.text:
logserv_filter_upgrade_check.py

Scripted input (runs every 600 seconds / 10 minutes):

  1. Compares current TA version against last-checked version (persisted in state file)
  2. On version change, discovers supported types from @logserv_filter annotations
  3. Compares against user’s include patterns (include_filters only — exclude patterns and both source fields are not part of the comparison; a list containing */* or * covers every type)
  4. Creates a Splunk system message banner if uncovered types are found
Performance

The version check is ~2ms on unchanged runs. Full comparison only runs once per version change.

docs.title: Filter Chain
docs.text:
All filtering happens via a single TRANSFORMS-00-filter line in local/props.conf under the [sap_logserv_logs] stanza. The TRANSFORMS-* classes run in ASCII order of their names, so the 00 prefix puts the filters before the metadata (01), sourcetype routing (02–09), stamp (50–51) and unwrap (99) transforms. Splunk’s props.conf specification documents only the order of the transforms inside one class; the order across classes is Splunk’s observed behaviour. See TRANSFORMS-00-filter Ordering for why the order matters.

The filter chain is evaluated left to right, and the last transform whose REGEX matches sets the queue:

# Stanza Generated when REGEX FORMAT 1 logserv_filter_include_drop include gate on . (every event) nullQueue 2 logserv_filter_include_allow include gate on folder includes indexQueue 3 logserv_filter_include_sources include gate on and include_sources not empty source includes indexQueue 4 logserv_filter_time_drop days_in_past > 0 epoch < cutoff nullQueue 5 logserv_filter_exclude exclude_filters not empty folder excludes nullQueue 6 logserv_filter_exclude_sources exclude_sources not empty source excludes nullQueue

This “deny-all, then allow” approach ensures only explicitly included events pass through, and placing the time filter and the excludes last makes them win over both include steps.

  • Include gate: on when the folder include list is not pass-all. The list is pass-all when it is empty or contains any */* or bare * entry; then stanzas 1–3 are not generated. Earlier builds treated only an exact ['*/*'] as pass-all — */*, x gated out every event without folder fields and a bare * was skipped. A bare * in exclude_filters still excludes nothing.
  • Include Sources while pass-all: refused by the handler at save time when filtering is enabled (“has no effect”); not generated, with a WARNING from generate_transforms_stanzas(), when it reaches the generators anyway (a refresh of a hand-edited conf).
  • Pass-all test: is_pass_all_include() (the old _is_wildcard_include name is kept as an alias). A dir/subdir entry whose segments are only * characters, such as **/*, counts as pass-all too.
  • Stanza layout: every generated stanza has the keys REGEX, FORMAT, DEST_KEY = queue and LOOKAHEAD = 100000, in that order (LOOKAHEAD last). Each name appears in the props line only when its stanza is generated, and every generated stanza is named in the props line.
  • Chunks: a long list is split over several stanzas (see Chunking). Chunk 1 keeps the plain name, chunk n ≥ 2 is <name>_<n> (logserv_filter_exclude_2, …), and all chunks of a list sit together at the list’s place in the line, so last-match-wins is unchanged.

The generated local/props.conf block (one line; names shown here for the case where every field is in use and the source exclude list needed two chunks):

[sap_logserv_logs]
TRANSFORMS-00-filter = logserv_filter_include_drop, logserv_filter_include_allow, logserv_filter_include_sources, logserv_filter_time_drop, logserv_filter_exclude, logserv_filter_exclude_sources, logserv_filter_exclude_sources_2

And one generated local/transforms.conf stanza (Exclude Sources /var/log/zypper.log):

[logserv_filter_exclude_sources]
REGEX = (?:^|"_raw"\s*:\s*"(?:[^"\\]++|\\.)*+")(?:(?=(?:(?!"_raw")[^\n])*?"source"\s*:\s*"\/var\/log\/zypper\.log"))
FORMAT = nullQueue
DEST_KEY = queue
LOOKAHEAD = 100000

The filter transforms run at TRANSFORMS-00, before TRANSFORMS-01-metadata (extract_host, extract_source, extract_clz), so they match the raw envelope text — the "source", "clz_dir" and "clz_subdir" keys of the NDJSON line — not MetaData:Source or the indexed fields.

docs.title: Filter Regex Generation
docs.text:
Folder patterns (include_filters, exclude_filters) and source patterns (include_sources, exclude_sources) are translated by one hand-written translator. fnmatch.translate is never used: its output changed in Python 3.13, its Python 3.14 output cannot be unwrapped, and its * (.*) ran past the end of the JSON value into later keys or the _raw text. The exact generated text — byte-exact, because the App’s Data Doctor parses generated transforms.conf back into patterns and its check:diagnostics gate pins this shape:

SKIP          = (?:^|"_raw"\s*:\s*"(?:[^"\\]++|\\.)*+")
LA(key, frag) = (?=(?:(?!"_raw")[^\n])*?"key"\s*:\s*"frag")
split p on runs of '*'  ->  segments S0, S1, ..., Sk   (k = number of star RUNS; '**' counts as one '*')
seg(S)  : per character - ? -> [^"]   [A-Za-z0-9_] -> itself   any other allowed character c -> backslash + c
k = 0   : f(p) = seg(S0)
k >= 1  : f(p) = seg(S0) + (?>[^"]*?seg(S1)) + ... + (?>[^"]*?seg(S(k-1))) + [^"]* + seg(Sk)
folder   d/s    -> LA(clz_dir, f(d)) LA(clz_subdir, f(s))
source   p      -> LA(source, f(p))
combined d/s=p  -> LA(clz_dir, f(d)) LA(clz_subdir, f(s)) LA(source, f(p))
REGEX of a chunk = SKIP + "(?:" + entries joined by "|" + ")"

SKIP is FILTER_REGEX_SKIP and the gap inside LA is FILTER_REGEX_GAP. In seg, the characters / . - : + @ ~ become \/ \. \- \: \+ \@ \~. A run of * is one or more * in a row; every run before the last becomes an atomic group, so the cost stays linear (see Linear Wildcard Matching). Golden examples (one entry each):

linux/linux_secure      (?:^|"_raw"\s*:\s*"(?:[^"\\]++|\\.)*+")(?:(?=(?:(?!"_raw")[^\n])*?"clz_dir"\s*:\s*"linux")(?=(?:(?!"_raw")[^\n])*?"clz_subdir"\s*:\s*"linux_secure"))
/var/log/zypper.log     (?:^|"_raw"\s*:\s*"(?:[^"\\]++|\\.)*+")(?:(?=(?:(?!"_raw")[^\n])*?"source"\s*:\s*"\/var\/log\/zypper\.log"))
hana/*                  (?:^|"_raw"\s*:\s*"(?:[^"\\]++|\\.)*+")(?:(?=(?:(?!"_raw")[^\n])*?"clz_dir"\s*:\s*"hana")(?=(?:(?!"_raw")[^\n])*?"clz_subdir"\s*:\s*"[^"]*"))
/var/log/YaST2/*        (?:^|"_raw"\s*:\s*"(?:[^"\\]++|\\.)*+")(?:(?=(?:(?!"_raw")[^\n])*?"source"\s*:\s*"\/var\/log\/YaST2\/[^"]*"))
linux/linux_secure=/var/log/zypper.log
                        (?:^|"_raw"\s*:\s*"(?:[^"\\]++|\\.)*+")(?:(?=(?:(?!"_raw")[^\n])*?"clz_dir"\s*:\s*"linux")(?=(?:(?!"_raw")[^\n])*?"clz_subdir"\s*:\s*"linux_secure")(?=(?:(?!"_raw")[^\n])*?"source"\s*:\s*"\/var\/log\/zypper\.log"))

Golden examples with more than one * (source entries; the whole chunk REGEX):

/usr/sap/*/trace/*             (?:^|"_raw"\s*:\s*"(?:[^"\\]++|\\.)*+")(?:(?=(?:(?!"_raw")[^\n])*?"source"\s*:\s*"\/usr\/sap\/(?>[^"]*?\/trace\/)[^"]*"))
*zypper*                       (?:^|"_raw"\s*:\s*"(?:[^"\\]++|\\.)*+")(?:(?=(?:(?!"_raw")[^\n])*?"source"\s*:\s*"(?>[^"]*?zypper)[^"]*"))
/usr/sap/*/HDB*/*/trace/*.trc  (?:^|"_raw"\s*:\s*"(?:[^"\\]++|\\.)*+")(?:(?=(?:(?!"_raw")[^\n])*?"source"\s*:\s*"\/usr\/sap\/(?>[^"]*?\/HDB)(?>[^"]*?\/)(?>[^"]*?\/trace\/)[^"]*\.trc"))
/var/log/**/x.log              (?:^|"_raw"\s*:\s*"(?:[^"\\]++|\\.)*+")(?:(?=(?:(?!"_raw")[^\n])*?"source"\s*:\s*"\/var\/log\/[^"]*\/x\.log"))

How the shape works:

  • Whole-value, case-sensitive matching. Each condition ends with the value’s closing ", so a pattern matches the whole value. ? becomes [^"], and a run of * becomes [^"]* or, before the last run, a lazy [^"]*? inside an atomic group, so a wildcard can never leave its JSON value; a source * crosses / (it is still inside the value). The generated PCRE does not fold case.
  • Where the search starts. In Azure and GCP envelopes source, clz_dir and clz_subdir sit before _raw; in AWS envelopes after it (_raw, _time, host, source, clzfilename, clz_dir, clz_subdir). In both layouts the metadata keys are grouped and never separated by _raw. SKIP therefore anchors either at the line start or right after the _raw value — the same possessive skip [set_raw_only] ships with — and each condition is a lookahead whose gap may not run past a "_raw" key, so text inside the event is never searched for envelope keys. JSON escaping inside _raw puts a backslash before every quote, so an unescaped "key" cannot match there anyway. An envelope that puts _raw between the keys one entry needs does not match that entry: a folder entry needs clz_dir and clz_subdir, and a combined entry also source, on the same side of _raw. A plain source entry needs only source, which one of the two starts always reaches, so it still matches (split envelopes have never been seen).
  • Order-free conditions. The lookaheads of one entry may match in any key order.
  • Plain source entries reach events without folder fields; folder and combined entries need both clz_dir and clz_subdir.
  • The time stanza keeps its unanchored "_time" epoch regex and gains LOOKAHEAD = 100000.
Why this shape — Splunk PCRE probes

Every candidate was run on Splunk’s own PCRE as rex field=line "(?<h>REGEX)" with match_limit = 100000 and depth_limit = 1000 (the transforms.conf MATCH_LIMIT / DEPTH_LIMIT defaults), over synthetic envelopes of 177 and 99,162 bytes in the AWS order, the clz-first order and a split order, with and without JSON-escaped quotes in _raw, matching and non-matching:

Candidate Result The old anchored shape ^(?=.*K1)(?=.*K2), greedy or lazy FATAL “has exceeded configured match_limit” Unanchored two-key alternation in both orders Correct The same with three keys (six orders) FATAL match_limit Six orders with a gap that stops at "_raw", 21 entries FATAL “regular expression is too large” SKIP + lookaheads: folder, source, combined, 40- and 80-entry lists Correct on every envelope Unanchored "source" condition; the time regex Correct

So raising LOOKAHEAD alone would have broken the existing filters on long lines: the shape had to change with it. Any change to the shape needs the same kind of check on Splunk’s PCRE, on lines close to 100,000 characters, matching and non-matching, in every envelope order.

docs.title: Linear Wildcard Matching
docs.text:
The rule gives every run of * before the last the form (?>[^"]*?seg): the regex engine places the segment that follows the run at its leftmost occurrence in the value, and because the group is atomic it never goes back to try a later one. Only the last run, [^"]*, backtracks, and only one level deep. The work to match a source, clz_dir or clz_subdir value therefore grows linearly with the length of the value, however many * the pattern has. The same rule applies to source patterns and to the dir and subdir parts of folder patterns.

Why. Translating every * to [^"]* makes the engine try every way of dividing the value among the stars: a pattern with k runs of * takes about nk steps on a value of n characters that it does not match. On Splunk’s PCRE2, with the transforms.conf default MATCH_LIMIT of 100,000, that translation exceeded the limit for *a*a*b through *a*a*a*a*a*a*b on a source of / and 150 a characters, for /var/log/********x on /var/log/ and 80 y characters, and for */*/*/*/*/*.x and */*/*/*/*/*/*/*.x on a path with 17 slashes: the search-time rex used for the check stopped with a match-limit error. At index time a filter REGEX that exceeds the limit is expected to count as no match (this has not been measured on a forwarder), so an Exclude rule would silently keep the event and an Include rule would drop it, and whether that happens depends on the source values in the data, not only on the pattern. Realistic patterns (up to four * with distinctive text between them) stayed inside the limit, but nothing guaranteed it.

Same matches. The segments between runs have a fixed length (a ? is one character), so placing a middle segment at its leftmost occurrence never loses a match that a later placement would find. Checked on 54,974 random pattern and value pairs against a glob oracle, with no disagreement, and on Splunk’s PCRE2: 16 of 16 patterns gave the oracle’s result on all 50 envelopes each, with no match-limit message, among them six of the eight patterns that had exceeded the limit (*a*a*b, *a*a*a*a*a*b, *a*a*a*a*a*a*b, /var/log/********x, */*/*/*/*/*.x, */*/*/*/*/*/*/*.x).

Runs count once. ** produces the same text as *, so the generated text cannot tell them apart. The App’s Data Doctor, which reads generated transforms.conf back into patterns, therefore shows each run of * as a single *: /var/log/**/x.log appears as /var/log/*/x.log, which matches the same values.

docs.title: Chunking
docs.text: Each list is de-duplicated (first occurrence kept, order preserved). Entries are added to the current chunk until the next entry would take its REGEX past FILTER_REGEX_MAX_CHARS (8,000 characters); that entry starts a new chunk. Splunk’s PCRE compiled an 80-entry combined list (12,765 characters) in this shape, but refused a 16,000-character REGEX of an earlier candidate shape as “regular expression is too large”, so 8,000 leaves a margin. A single entry whose alternative alone would pass the limit is refused with a message naming the entry.

docs.title: Python Compatibility
docs.text: The possessive quantifiers in SKIP and the atomic groups of the * rule need Python 3.11+ re, but the shipped code never compiles a generated REGEX: it is text written to a conf file and run by Splunk’s PCRE. The module must import and run on Splunk’s Python 3.9 as well as 3.13 (python.required = 3.13), because the persistent settings handler, Deploy to Forwarders, the S3 Direct stamp handler and both scripted inputs import it. Tests compile the REGEX on 3.13 / 3.14. On 3.8 / 3.9, which have neither, they replace the possessive body of SKIP with an atomic-group emulation ((?=((?:[^"\\]+|\\.)*))\1): the same matches, without the catastrophic backtracking a plain ++ -> + copy shows on 3.8. Each atomic group (?>X) of the * rule is emulated the same way, as (?=(X))\N, with N numbered left to right after the group of the SKIP emulation.

docs.title: Validation Layers
docs.text:
A value reaches a conf file through three paths — the UCC REST write, the RestError[403] filesystem fallback (update_local_stanza()), and a hand edit — so the source fields are checked in three places:

  1. Splunk Web / UCC. globalConfig.json defines include_sources and exclude_sources as text entities after exclude_filters (so days_in_past, the hook’s anchor, stays last) with a string validator (at most 4,096 characters) and a regex validator ^[A-Za-z0-9/._:*?=,+@~ -]*$. UCC runs them in the browser and in the generated rh_settings.py before the REST write — before a 403 can reach the fallback, whether filtering is on or off. They are not enough on their own: empty values skip validators, and Python’s re.match lets $ accept a trailing newline.
  2. The REST handler. The full grammar runs on every save for the two source fields, even with filtering disabled, because their values are written to a conf either way; a stray ", \ or newline would otherwise reach a conf line or a REGEX. Every other posted value (include_filters, exclude_filters, filter_enabled, days_in_past, and any unexpected key) is checked on every save too, for conf safety only: no control character, tab included, and no trailing backslash (_validate_posted_values()), so the 403 fallback cannot write a line break into the settings conf. The folder patterns and Days in the Past are checked against their grammar when filtering is enabled, as before, together with the pass-all rule for Include Sources and a dry run of the generators, so a value they would refuse is refused before anything is saved.
  3. The generators. generate_transforms_stanzas() / generate_props_filter_lines() re-validate every entry and raise on an invalid one, whatever path the value came by: the handler refuses the save, and the daily refresh logs an ERROR and keeps the last good block (see Daily Time Refresh).

The source grammar:

list    := entry ("," entry)*            (spaces around entries are stripped; any other whitespace is rejected; empty entries rejected)
entry   := srcpat | folder "=" srcpat
folder  := dir "/" subdir                (as Include/Exclude Filters: [A-Za-z0-9*?._:-]+ per segment; no bare *)
srcpat  := 1..512 of [A-Za-z0-9/._:*?+@~-], with at least one character that is not * ? or /

Rejected characters: " \ , (the list separator) = (inside a source pattern) whitespace [ ], control characters and non-ASCII. Rejected source patterns: *, **, /*, */* — anything that would match everything.

docs.title: AWS S3 Direct Filter Preview
docs.text: appserver/static/logserv_s3_direct.js decides which folders a backfill leaves out because this forwarder’s filters would drop their events. It mirrors the generator’s folder matching — per segment, case-sensitive, * and ? as wildcards, and the pass-all rule — instead of the prefix comparison it used before, which left out every folder under the default */* and never matched a pattern such as */cron. Source rules act on single files, so the preview cannot decide them per folder: they never change a folder’s verdict, they only add a note — “some files may be kept by Include Sources” on a folder the include gate leaves out, “some files may be dropped by Exclude Sources” on a planned folder — as the App’s Data Doctor marks its folder verdicts approximate. A stored value the generator would refuse is reported first (the forwarder then keeps the rules it generated last, which the screen cannot see). The preview reads this forwarder’s stored settings; on a forwarder whose Data TA a Deployment Server manages they can be older than the pushed rules (only transforms.conf and props.conf are mirrored to deployment-apps/), and a plan with a source note says so.

docs.title: Time Filter Regex
docs.text:
The time filter matches epoch timestamps in the raw JSON "_time" field. A TRANSFORMS REGEX is fixed text and cannot compute “N days ago” when an event arrives, so the cutoff is a pre-computed regex that matches epoch values less than the cutoff. This regex must be refreshed daily to maintain accuracy. Its stanza, like every generated filter stanza, sets LOOKAHEAD = 100000.

Failure mode

If the daily refresh doesn’t run, the cutoff is not advanced: it stays one day further in the past for each missed day, so the filter drops slightly less data — up to one extra day of older events per missed day is kept — until the next refresh or Save.

docs.title: Why TRANSFORMS Instead of INGEST_EVAL
docs.text: The Data TA filters with TRANSFORMS-based queue routing (REGEX, FORMAT = nullQueue or indexQueue, DEST_KEY = queue, LOOKAHEAD), not with INGEST_EVAL. This is a design constraint of the project, recorded as “INGEST_EVAL is unavailable on Splunk Cloud heavy forwarders”. That premise has not been re-checked against Splunk’s current documentation, so treat it as the project’s choice rather than as a statement about what a Splunk platform supports. A change to INGEST_EVAL would also have to keep the generated transforms.conf shape that the App’s Data Doctor parses back (see Filter Regex Generation).

docs.title: DS Detection
docs.text:
Two-step detection in is_deployment_server():

  1. Fast path — Check server_roles from /services/server/info for deployment_server
  2. Fallback — If role is absent, query /services/deployment/server/clients to check for connected deployment clients. Returns true only if at least one client is connected
Why the fallback exists

Splunk removes the deployment_server role from server_roles when no server class is defined in any serverclass.conf, so a fresh DS has no role yet. /services/deployment/server/clients returns 0 clients on HFs (no false positives) and returns the connected clients on a real DS even without any server classes. The /services/deployment/server/config endpoint cannot be used as a fallback because it returns HTTP 200 on ALL Splunk Enterprise instances (including HFs), causing false positives.

docs.title: Server Class Creation
docs.text:
ensure_serverclass() creates SAP_LogServ_HeavyForwarders in three steps:

  1. REST API create — POST to /services/deployment/server/serverclasses with name parameter to create the server class

    The disabled parameter is NOT supported during creation (Splunk returns an error).

  2. REST API disable — Separate POST to /services/deployment/server/serverclasses/SAP_LogServ_HeavyForwarders with disabled=true to disable the server class. This ensures no deployment occurs until the admin configures client targeting and enables the server class in Forwarder Management.

  3. File-based app mapping — After REST creates and disables the server class, the function locates the resulting serverclass.conf (which Splunk may write to system/local/ or apps/search/local/) and appends the app mapping stanza:

[serverClass:SAP_LogServ_HeavyForwarders:app:splunk_ta_sap_logserv]
restartSplunkd = true
stateOnClient = enabled

Note

The app mapping cannot be created via REST API — the URL path format serverclasses/{name}/app:{appname} returns HTTP 404.

docs.title: Deployment-Apps Sync
docs.text:
ensure_deployment_app_synced() runs on a DS after every Save on the Filters or Cloud Provider tab, and in the daily time refresh. It copies the full package from etc/apps/splunk_ta_sap_logserv/ (including that copy’s local/) to etc/deployment-apps/splunk_ta_sap_logserv/ in two cases only:

  1. First copy: deployment-apps/splunk_ta_sap_logserv/ does not exist yet.
  2. Version change: the [launcher] version in default/app.conf differs between the two copies. The deployment-apps/ copy is deleted and copied again.

When the versions are equal it copies nothing. mirror_to_deployment_apps() then copies only local/transforms.conf and local/props.conf. Two consequences:

  • Every 0.1.2 build has [launcher] version = 0.1.2; builds differ only in [install] build, which is not compared. A newer build with the same version installed in etc/apps/ is not copied, so the heavy forwarders keep the older code and default/ files and receive only the new filter rules. Update deployment-apps/ by hand, as Upgrading describes.
  • A copy made because of a version change deletes anything added by hand under deployment-apps/splunk_ta_sap_logserv/local/ that etc/apps/.../local/ does not have.

Deploy to Forwarders copies nothing; it only reloads the Deployment Server.

docs.title: Deployment Client Guard
docs.text: The logserv_filter_time_refresh.py scripted input checks whether the instance is a deployment client but not a Deployment Server. If so, it skips the refresh when the Deployment Server delivered the Data TA ($SPLUNK_HOME/var/run/serverclass.xml lists splunk_ta_sap_logserv) or when that record is missing, unreadable or lists no app. Without this guard, a heavy forwarder would read its own empty local settings on the daily run, regenerate the configs with only a time filter, and overwrite the complete filter chain pushed by the DS. A deployment client that holds the Data TA directly (its serverclass.xml lists other apps but not the Data TA, for example a search head that is a deployment client for other apps) refreshes its own filter, as a single instance does.

docs.title: Step 1: Add a Routing Transform
docs.text:
Add the @logserv_filter annotation on the line immediately above the stanza header in default/transforms.conf:

# @logserv_filter: newdir/newsubdir
[set_srctype_for_new_logtype]
REGEX = "clz_subdir":"newsubdir"
FORMAT = sourcetype::sap:newlogtype
DEST_KEY = MetaData:Sourcetype
LOOKAHEAD = 100000

The annotation is critical. It declares which clz_dir/clz_subdir values the transform handles. Without it, the upgrade check cannot detect that a new log type is supported, and users won’t be notified.

Multiple values can be comma-separated:

# @logserv_filter: newdir/type_a, newdir/type_b, newdir/type_c
[set_srctype_for_new_dir]
REGEX = "clz_subdir":"(type_a|type_b|type_c)"
FORMAT = sourcetype::sap:newdir:logs
DEST_KEY = MetaData:Sourcetype
LOOKAHEAD = 100000

When the same clz_subdir value exists under multiple clz_dir paths (e.g., audit appears under both abap/ and scc/), key the route on both folder fields with the filter generator’s shape: its REGEX is byte-equal to the Include Filters REGEX of that one folder, fnmatch_patterns_to_combined_regex(['scc/audit']) in splunk_ta_sap_logserv_filter_utils.py (see Filter Regex Generation):

# @logserv_filter: scc/audit
[set_srctype_scc_audit]
REGEX = (?:^|"_raw"\s*:\s*"(?:[^"\\]++|\\.)*+")(?:(?=(?:(?!"_raw")[^\n])*?"clz_dir"\s*:\s*"scc")(?=(?:(?!"_raw")[^\n])*?"clz_subdir"\s*:\s*"audit"))
FORMAT = sourcetype::sap:scc:audit
DEST_KEY = MetaData:Sourcetype
LOOKAHEAD = 100000

When to key on both folders: Check if the clz_subdir you are adding already exists in another clz_dir path. If it does, both the existing and new transforms must key on both folder fields. Current collision-prone values include audit (abap, scc), sapstartsrv (abap, sap), tracelogs (hana, scc) and icm (abap; the Web Dispatcher’s webdispatcher/icm is a Secondary folder the Data TA leaves unrouted - builds of 2026-10-13 and earlier keyed the ICM route on clz_subdir alone and typed it sap:abap:icm).

Give every routing stanza LOOKAHEAD = 100000, and never pair a (?=.*...) lookahead with it. The AWS envelope puts _raw first (_raw, _time, host, source, clzfilename, clz_dir, clz_subdir), so with Splunk’s default window of 4,096 characters an AWS event longer than about 4 KB kept the input’s own host and source, got no folder fields and stayed sap_logserv_logs; every Data TA build up to the one of 2026-10-13 had that limit. A route on one literal key is a linear scan at any window, as long as nothing repeated in it can run past the value’s closing quote: the BIND routes match a path segment with [^\/"] for that reason, because with [^\/] the segment loop ran on through the rest of the line, one nested PCRE frame per slash against DEPTH_LIMIT; the Windows and sssd routes use [^"]* where they had .*, which ran on into the event text and, where PCRE2’s . stops at a Unicode line separator, backtracked over it. A route on two keys needs the generator’s shape: it starts only at the line start or just after the _raw value, skips that value possessively and never crosses a _raw key, so its work grows linearly with the line. The older form (?s)^(?=.*"clz_dir":"X")(?=.*"clz_subdir":"Y") reads the whole window in each lookahead, and near 100,000 characters it exceeds Splunk’s match limit (see the probes under Filter Regex Generation). Without the ^ it was worse: PCRE retried it at every character of a line it did not match, so the work grew with the square of the line length, and MATCH_LIMIT, which counts the work of each start position on its own, never stopped it. Every Data TA version from 0.0.4 to the 0.1.2 build of 2026-10-09 shipped those routes unanchored; the build of 2026-10-13 added (?s)^ (179 to 1,778 times faster at search time on lines of 460 to 4,160 characters), and the build of 2026-10-16 (1792189743) moved them to the generator’s shape with the 100,000-character window.

docs.title: Step 2: Add to TRANSFORMS Chain
docs.text:
Add your new transform to the appropriate TRANSFORMS-* line in the [sap_logserv_logs] stanza of default/props.conf:

[sap_logserv_logs]
...
TRANSFORMS-10-srctype_for_newdir = set_srctype_for_new_logtype

Pick the next free number in 10–49 for the TRANSFORMS prefix. Current allocation: 00 = filters, 01 = metadata (extract_host, extract_source, extract_clz), 02–09 = sourcetype routing (all in use), 50–51 = indexed-field stamps (splunk_solution, cloud_provider), 99 = set_raw_only.

docs.title: Step 3: Add Sourcetype Configuration
docs.text: If the new sourcetype needs field extractions, calculated fields, or CIM field aliases, add a [sap:newlogtype] stanza to default/props.conf.

docs.title: Step 4: Bump the Version
docs.text:
Bump meta.version in globalConfig.json — ucc-gen stamps it into the built default/app.conf, which is what get_ta_version() reads (it falls back to app.manifest only when app.conf is absent, i.e. before the UCC build). Keep package/app.manifest in sync so source and artifact agree. The version change triggers the upgrade check to compare the new annotations against existing user include patterns.

What Happens on Upgrade
  1. The logserv_filter_upgrade_check.py scripted input detects the version change within 10 minutes
  2. It scans the updated default/transforms.conf for @logserv_filter annotations
  3. If the user’s include patterns don’t cover the new log types, a system message banner appears across all Splunk Web pages
  4. The user updates their include patterns (or uses */*) and the banner clears

docs.title: Routing Data Without Folder Fields
docs.text:
Some LogServ data arrives without clz_dir and clz_subdir: SAP files it in a storage folder named undefined/undefined (see Data Delivered Without Folder Fields), and no folder route can match it. The Data TA routes one such kind, the HANA trace directory, by the envelope’s source path, as the last entry of TRANSFORMS-08-srctype_for_scc_and_hana_trace, after the folder route set_srctype_hana_tracelogs:

[set_srctype_hana_tracelogs_by_source]
REGEX = ^(?!(?>[^"]+|"_raw"\s*:\s*"(?:[^"\\]++|\\.)*+"|")*?"clz_subdir"\s*:)(?=(?>[^"]+|"_raw"\s*:\s*"(?:[^"\\]++|\\.)*+"|")*?"source"\s*:\s*"\/usr\/sap\/[A-Z0-9]{3}\/HDB\d{2}\/[^"\/]+\/trace\/(?:DB_[^"\/]+\/)?(?:[^"\/]+\.trc|backup\.log)")
FORMAT = sourcetype::sap:hana:tracelogs
DEST_KEY = MetaData:Sourcetype
LOOKAHEAD = 100000
  • Why it exists. In the LogServ deliveries examined when the route was written, all of the real HANA trace data — the .trc files and backup.log of /usr/sap/<SID>/HDB<nn>/<host>/trace/ and trace/DB_<tenant>/ — arrived without folder fields. [set_srctype_hana_tracelogs] keys on clz_dir=hana and clz_subdir=tracelogs, so it never matched real data (only the synthetic events of the Demo Data Generator TA, splunk_ta_sap_logserv_demo_gen, carry that folder; it is an internal tool that generates LogServ-shaped events for testing and demos, and it is not part of the release), and the trace files stayed sap_logserv_logs.
  • What it matches. The whole source value in the envelope: /usr/sap/, a three-character SID of upper-case letters and digits, HDB and two digits, one host folder, trace/, optionally one DB_<tenant>/ folder, then a .trc file or backup.log. Other files in those folders (backint.log, .trc.gz), deeper subfolders, a lower-case SID, a path written with \/ escapes and source text inside the escaped _raw (where every quote has a backslash before it) do not match and keep sap_logserv_logs.
  • The guard. The negative lookahead at the start, (?!(?>...)*?"clz_subdir"\s*:), limits the route to envelopes without a clz_subdir key — only when there are no folder fields. Like the source condition, it walks the line from its start over whole tokens - a run of characters without a quote, the _raw key with its whole value (skipped possessively, as [set_raw_only] does), or one quote - inside an atomic group, so it sees every envelope key on either side of _raw, never the event text, and its work grows linearly with the line. As the last entry of class 08 the route would otherwise win over every route of classes 02–08 for any event whose path matched; with the guard, an event that has folder fields is routed by its folder exactly as before. The class 09 routes (sap/*) all need "clz_subdir":"...", so none can match an event the guard lets through: the source route is final for it. The guard tests for the key, not its value: an envelope written with "clz_subdir":"" or "clz_subdir":null is not routed. The index shows only that the real events had no non-empty folder value; that their envelopes carry no clz_subdir key at all still has to be confirmed on one raw undefined/undefined blob.
  • LOOKAHEAD. 100,000 characters, like every routing stanza: the window [extract_source] reads, so an event is routed here only when its indexed source holds the path the App reads the SID, instance, host and tenant from. Builds of 2026-10-13 and earlier left both at the default 4,096 and scanned the line character by character (^(?![^\n]*?"clz_subdir"\s*:)[^\n]*?"source"...): on an AWS-order envelope whose _raw ran past that window neither matched, and the event stayed sap_logserv_logs with the input’s own source. At 100,000 characters that form exceeds the match limit, so the shape changed with the window; the matches did not. The route also accepts spaces around the colon, which [extract_source] does not; no real envelope has them.
  • No @logserv_filter annotation. An annotation declares the folders a route handles, and every reader treats it as a folder: the upgrade coverage check compares the folders with Include Filters, the AWS S3 Direct screen plans its inputs per folder, and the App’s SOURCETYPE_CLZ_MAP, which check:diagnostics re-derives from the annotations, gives the Data Doctor its kept/dropped verdicts. These events have no folder, and folder filters can neither keep nor drop them; only Include Sources and Exclude Sources reach them. Annotating the stanza hana/tracelogs would change none of those lists — the folder route declares it already, and both annotation parsers de-duplicate — but it would claim that the folder decides these events. The stanza’s comment says why it has none. The gate’s derivation reads only annotated stanzas, so it skips this one.
  • Filters and history. The filters run in TRANSFORMS-00, before routing, so the route changes no filter decision. Routing is index-time: events indexed before the Data TA update keep sap_logserv_logs.
  • Demo Data Generator lockstep. The Demo Data Generator’s fidelity.ROUTING mirrors the Data TA routing, and its fidelity test compares the two. It carries the forms of this Data TA build, and its compile_routing() rewrites the possessive quantifiers and atomic groups, which need Python 3.11, into forms with the same matches for the Python 3.9 of Splunk 9.4. Every Demo Data Generator HANA trace template carries the hana/tracelogs folder, so no generated output changes. Its per-input switch Send through the SAP LogServ Data TA (off by default) sends the producer’s line instead, as sap_logserv_logs, so the Data TA on a heavy forwarder routes and stamps those events as it does real data; the fidelity test replays this Data TA’s own files over the exact bytes sent, and every such event carries the indexed marker demo_gen=splunk_ta_sap_logserv_demo_gen. With the switch off, events arrive already sourcetyped, so the receiving Splunk’s own props for that sourcetype run as well: for linux_messages_syslog the built-in syslog-host transform takes the host from the syslog header, while an event this Data TA routes to that sourcetype keeps the envelope’s host. The generator therefore writes the event’s host into that header in both paths, and its fidelity test replays the built-in rule.

The other data delivered without folder fields, the Unix command output (ps, top, netstat, …), is deliberately left unrouted: it is not a LogServ log type, and each event holds a single table row, a header line or a table whose line breaks are the two characters \n, which no sourcetype the solution ships parses.

docs.title: LogServ Azure and GCP Add-on Internals
