docs.title: Splunk Cloud Considerations
docs.text:
Read this page before you install Splunk for SAP LogServ where the search tier, or the whole deployment, is Splunk Cloud Platform. It covers where each package goes, how to install a private app, which Splunk Cloud roles can configure the packages, and the capability checks that can refuse a write.

Splunk assigns each Splunk Cloud Platform stack one of two Experiences, Victoria or Classic; an Experience is not a version. To find yours, in Splunk Web click Support & Services → About. These notes were checked on one Splunk Cloud Platform 10.x stack, most recently on 10.5.2605.10 (2026-10-21). That stack is taken to be on the Victoria Experience, but its Experience was not read from Support & Services → About. No test on a stack known to be on the Classic Experience is recorded.

docs.title: Splunk Enterprise: what still applies
docs.text:
If you run Splunk Enterprise and your admins use Splunk’s stock admin role, which holds admin_all_objects, nothing on this page needs a workaround. These items still apply on Splunk Enterprise:

  • The audit capability. A user’s AI Assistant activity is audited only when their role holds edit_tcp or edit_log_alert_event (the /receivers/simple row below). Splunk Enterprise’s default admin role holds both, power holds edit_log_alert_event, and user holds neither.
  • admin_all_objects for Azure and GCP inputs and AWS S3 Direct backfills: creating, editing or deleting a LogServ Azure or GCP input (replacing its SAS or service-account key included), and Create backfill on the AWS S3 Direct screen, which without it offers only the Apply this as an administrator view: it generates the configuration but creates nothing. A hardened admin role that lacks the capability is refused these too.
  • The filesystem fallback for Data TA Configuration saves, which serves any role in the write list that lacks admin_all_objects, a hardened admin role included.
  • The edit_deployment_server check on Deploy to Forwarders, on your own Deployment Server (below).
  • The admin-tier write lists on the LogServ App’s KV Store collections. They apply on every platform (Application Settings).

docs.title: Where the packages go with Splunk Cloud
docs.text:
The full matrix is Where Each Package Goes. With Splunk Cloud:

Where What to install Splunk Cloud search head The LogServ App and its search-tier add-ons (LogServ App Prerequisites). Splunk Cloud indexes Create sap_logserv_logs and logserv_ai_assistant_audit yourself, with the retention you want, before any data arrives: Settings → Indexes → New Index, or the Admin Config Service (ACS). See Create the indexes. Your heavy forwarders (Splunk Enterprise instances you run) The Data TA and the ingest add-on for your cloud: the Splunk Add-on for AWS, the LogServ Azure add-on or the LogServ GCP add-on. They send to the stack with its universal forwarder credentials app. If a Deployment Server manages the forwarders, install the Data TA on the Deployment Server only and push it from there (Distribute the Data TA to Heavy Forwarders); without one, install it directly on each forwarder. Install the Azure and GCP add-ons directly on the forwarders that run their inputs, never through the Deployment Server.

Notes:

  • Retention counts from each event’s time. Splunk freezes a bucket when its newest event is older than the index’s retention, so history you load later with AWS S3 Direct is removed soon after indexing if the index keeps less than its age. Set Searchable retention (days) to cover the oldest day you will load.
  • The Data TA on the Cloud stack is allowed, and needed only where the inputs run on the search head.
  • Splunk Cloud with no heavy forwarder is supported: it is not blocked, but a heavy forwarder is strongly recommended. On the stack these notes were checked on, installing the Data TA and the LogServ App on the search head and opening the AWS S3 Direct screen there have been checked; creating and running inputs there has not been tested. On the Classic Experience, inputs run on an Inputs Data Manager (IDM) rather than the search head; that path has not been tested (Where Each Package Goes). On Victoria the LogServ App, the Data TA and the ingest add-on all go on the Cloud search head, and the inputs run there, so the search tier your users search on also carries the ingest load, including the first-start backlog. The LogServ Azure and GCP add-ons declare search-head support, but running them on a Splunk Cloud search head has not been tested. See Running the TAs on a search head.

docs.title: Installing the packages on Splunk Cloud
docs.text:
The Splunk Add-on for AWS and the search-tier add-ons are on Splunkbase. The LogServ App, the Data TA and the LogServ Azure and GCP add-ons are private apps: download their tarballs from the repository’s release_binaries/ and upload them.

  • Victoria Experience: in Splunk Web, Apps → Manage Apps → Install app from file, or install with ACS. Splunk vets each upload before it installs it. Splunk’s steps: Install a private app on Victoria Experience.
  • Classic Experience: follow Install a private app on Classic Experience.

Each LogServ package passes AppInspect’s Cloud checks (--mode precert --included-tags cloud) with no errors and no failures; the reports are beside the tarballs in release_binaries/. To update, upload the newer tarball the same way: a newer build with the same version number (0.1.2) installs over the installed one (checked on Splunk Cloud Platform 10.5.2605.10).

You cannot edit files under an app’s local/ on Splunk Cloud. Use these Splunk Web screens instead of the local/ edits other pages describe:

Setting Where in Splunk Web Indexes and their retention Settings → Indexes Which indexes a role can search Settings → Roles → role → Indexes Filters and the Cloud Provider value (where the Data TA runs on the search head) Apps → Splunk TA for SAP LogServ → Configuration History loads from AWS Apps → Splunk TA for SAP LogServ → AWS S3 Direct (AWS S3 Direct) The data index macro after a rename Settings → Advanced search → Search macros, sap_logserv_idx_macro, in each LogServ app that has it (Renaming an Index) Disabling or re-scheduling the LogServ App’s scheduled searches Settings → Searches, reports, and alerts AI Assistant and Dashboard Data settings the LogServ App’s Settings pages (Application Settings)

One setting has no Splunk Web field: the _meta = cloud_provider::aws line on a Splunk Add-on for AWS SQS-Based S3 input that runs on the Cloud search head (the add-on’s SQS-Based S3 form has no field for it; checked on version 8.3.1). Without file access, set it with a REST write that needs admin_all_objects; see Splunk Cloud Without a Heavy Forwarder.

docs.title: Splunk Cloud roles
docs.text:
Role Who has it What it means for LogServ sc_admin The customer’s administrator role on Splunk Cloud Platform. Splunk gives it the capabilities to install apps, manage indexes, and manage users and passwords. The role you normally install and configure LogServ with. admin and the system-user roles Splunk, which uses them to monitor and maintain the stack. Do not change or delete them. sc_subadmin (only where your stack has one) Not a Splunk-supplied role. Some stacks create a delegated-admin role with this name. LogServ grants it write access by name and the App treats it as an admin. Its capabilities, admin_all_objects included, are whatever your stack gave it. power, user Standard roles. Search and view dashboards; cannot install or configure apps.

Check your role. In Settings → Users, look at the roles on your account. If you hold sc_admin, you are the stack administrator. If you hold a delegated-admin role (such as sc_subadmin), open it under Settings → Roles → role → Capabilities and check for admin_all_objects, edit_storage_passwords, and edit_tcp or edit_log_alert_event. The table below says what each one controls.

Only three role names count as admin

The LogServ App treats a user as an admin only when they hold a role named exactly admin, sc_admin or sc_subadmin, and the packages’ write lists in metadata/default.meta name only those three roles. A user whose delegated-admin role has any other name gets no Settings entry in the App’s menu, and opening the page shows 403 — Admin access required, so that user cannot change the AI Assistant settings or run Dashboard Data Clear and Backfill. Give such users one of the three roles itself; whether a role that only imports one of them is enough has not been tested. See Who Can Open the Page.

The AI Assistant also needs the Splunk MCP Server’s mcp_tool_execute capability, which the MCP Server grants by default only to admin and sc_admin. Add it to a delegated-admin role such as sc_subadmin and to every analyst role that will use the AI Assistant (Roles and Capabilities).

docs.title: Capability-gated REST endpoints
docs.text:
Splunk’s REST framework enforces some capability requirements server-side, independent of any per-object access control list. These gates decide what an admin role without admin_all_objects (a delegated admin on Splunk Cloud, or a hardened admin on Splunk Enterprise) can do with the LogServ packages; the /receivers/simple gate also decides whether each AI Assistant user is audited:

REST endpoint Gate LogServ usage /storage/passwords edit_storage_passwords HEC audit-forwarder tokens, MCP bearer tokens, and LLM provider credentials where the free-form path is used /storage/collections/data/<collection> None — collection-level metadata ACL only AI Assistant settings + acks, topology layouts, dashboard refresh preferences /configs/conf-<name>/... admin_all_objects (splunkd refuses the write with requires capability: admin_all_objects even when the app’s metadata gives the role write access) The Data TA’s Configuration tabs, which fall back to a direct file write on a 403 (below). The LogServ App keeps its AI Assistant settings in KV Store instead, to avoid this gate. /data/inputs/<service> admin_all_objects Creating, editing or deleting a LogServ Azure or GCP input on the add-on’s Inputs page, replacing its SAS or service-account key included. The input handler writes the input to data/inputs/<kind> as the signed-in user, and splunkd refuses that write to a role without the capability, so the save fails with HTTP 403 (“This operation is forbidden”), on any platform. The passSystemAuth = true line each add-on carries on its [admin_external:*] stanza has no effect: Splunk defines that setting only for [script:*] handlers. Create these inputs on a heavy forwarder (recommended), with a role that holds the capability. The Splunk Add-on for AWS input endpoint (/servicesNS/nobody/Splunk_TA_aws/splunk_ta_aws_aws_s3), and the Data TA’s s3_direct_meta handler, which writes configs/conf-inputs and disables and enables the new input through data/inputs/aws_s3 admin_all_objects: the screen checks for it before it offers Create backfill, and the handler’s configs/conf-inputs write is behind the /configs/conf-* gate above The Data TA’s AWS S3 Direct screen. Its writes run as the signed-in user, with no system-context bypass, by design. Without the capability the screen shows Apply this as an administrator with the generated configuration and creates nothing. On Splunk Cloud, sign in with an account that holds the capability and create the backfill on the screen; do not apply the generated configuration by hand. See AWS S3 Direct. /receivers/simple edit_tcp or edit_log_alert_event (on Splunk Enterprise the default admin role holds both, power holds edit_log_alert_event and user neither; on Splunk Cloud, check your roles as described above) AI Assistant audit events: the browser writes each one as the signed-in user, so a user without either capability is not audited and sees an Audit events are not being written warning in the AI Assistant panel. edit_log_alert_event is the narrower one to grant; either lets the role write events to any index, and edit_tcp also lets it change TCP data inputs — see Who Can Write Audit Events

The takeaway: write access in an app’s metadata does not get past these gates; a role without the capability gets 403. The LogServ packages avoid the gates where they can (the App keeps its settings in KV Store) or work around them (the Data TA’s Configuration saves fall back to a direct file write). Three actions they neither avoid nor bypass, on Splunk Cloud and Splunk Enterprise alike:

  • creating, editing or deleting a LogServ Azure or GCP input: admin_all_objects;
  • Create backfill on the AWS S3 Direct screen: admin_all_objects;
  • writing AI Assistant audit events on /receivers/simple: edit_tcp or edit_log_alert_event, checked for each user, so whether a user’s activity is audited depends on that user’s role.

docs.title: What the LogServ packages do for admin roles
docs.text: These are in the shipped packages and need no configuration.

docs.title: sc_subadmin in metadata/default.meta write ACL
docs.text:
Every LogServ package (the App, the Data TA, and the Azure and GCP add-ons) ships this global rule in metadata/default.meta: access = read : [ * ], write : [ admin, sc_admin, sc_subadmin ]. It gives the three roles write access to every knowledge object in the app (saved searches, macros, lookups, eventtypes, tags, etc.) at the metadata layer. The packages do not create sc_subadmin; they name it for stacks that have a delegated-admin role of that name. The App’s KV Store collections use the same three-role write list, apart from six that every user writes: four per-user preference collections and two Data Doctor collections. The App keeps the AI Assistant’s settings and legal acknowledgements in KV Store, which needs no admin_all_objects, and opens its Application Settings page only to the three role names; both are described in Application Settings.

If you rebuild the Data TA from source, the build step that keeps sc_subadmin in this list is described in Data TA Internals.

docs.title: Data TA Configuration saves fall back to the filesystem
docs.text: The Data TA’s Configuration → Filters and Cloud Provider tabs write their settings through splunktaucclib’s REST persist. If that write returns 403 (“This operation is forbidden” — the admin_all_objects gate on /configs/conf-*), the handler falls back to writing local/splunk_ta_sap_logserv_settings.conf directly on the filesystem, so Save succeeds for a role in the write list without admin_all_objects: a delegated admin role on Splunk Cloud, or a hardened admin role on Splunk Enterprise. Note passSystemAuth is not honoured for UCC [admin_external:*] settings handlers — the filesystem fallback is what actually carries these saves. The LogServ Azure and GCP add-ons have no such fallback (the /data/inputs/<service> row above).

docs.title: Deploy to Forwarders does not apply on Splunk Cloud
docs.text:
The Data TA’s Deploy to Forwarders button (Configuration → Filters and Cloud Provider) appears only on a Deployment Server, and a Splunk Cloud stack is never one. So the button does not appear on Splunk Cloud, for any role, and Splunk Cloud needs no capability for it. A Deployment Server for your heavy forwarders is a Splunk Enterprise instance you run yourself; your Splunk Cloud subscription includes a Deployment Server license, which you request from Splunk Support. See Distribute the Data TA to Heavy Forwarders.

On that Deployment Server, the button and the check that decides whether to show it need the edit_deployment_server capability, not admin_all_objects. Splunk Enterprise’s admin role holds it; a custom Deployment Server operator role needs it added, or the button does not appear.

docs.title: Splunk Cloud Support tickets you may need to file
docs.text: Symptom Ticket request AI Assistant SETUP REQUIRED banner; MCP requests return Invalid token audience: <X> Ask Splunk Cloud Support to set the stack’s MCP audience to mcp (Splunk MCP Setup) Your admin role cannot install private apps, or private-app vetting rejects one Standard Splunk Cloud private-app submission flow; out of scope for this guide Your delegated admin role needs admin_all_objects: the AWS S3 Direct screen shows Apply this as an administrator, or an Azure or GCP input save returns 403 Sign in with an account that holds admin_all_objects, or ask your stack’s administrator or Splunk Cloud Support whether your role can be given it

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Capacity Planning and First Start: size the instances that parse LogServ data, and plan for the backlog a new input finds in its queue.
  • Create the Indexes and Install the Data TA.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
SAP ECS environment logs are not a singular data source but a collection of OS-specific, SAP environment, database, and other application logs.

Due to the nature of this solution, the SAP LogServ packages are not standalone integrations. To take full advantage of their capabilities (like CIM mapping), install the search-tier add-ons listed in LogServ App Prerequisites.

For a streamlined data ingestion process, all selected logs are ingested under one sourcetype: sap_logserv_logs. The Data TA then assigns each event its final sourcetype during index-time parsing on the heavy forwarder (or the single instance). SAP application logs (HANA audit and trace, ABAP, Cloud Connector, SAP host services) are routed by their clz_dir / clz_subdir folder fields. Linux, ISC BIND (DNS), Squid (proxy), Windows and SAP Web Dispatcher access logs are routed by their source path, and so are HANA trace files delivered without folder fields. When both kinds of route match, the later one wins: /var/log/messages lines in the sap/saprouter folder become sap:saprouter.

All events are in NDJSON format with metadata (like _time, host, source, etc.) and the _raw field containing the event contents. To limit index size, only the _raw field is ingested from each event – metadata fields are either mapped to Splunk’s native metadata fields or dropped. However clz_dir and clz_subdir fields are preserved to maintain backtracking capabilities. These fields correspond to the directory tree of the original data in object storage.

The Data TA also stamps splunk_solution (always splunk_for_sap_logserv, identifying events that flowed through this solution) at index time on every routed event. Events can also carry an indexed cloud_provider field (aws, azure, or gcp, identifying the cloud the data was ingested from). The Azure and GCP ingest add-ons set it on every input. For AWS, add _meta = cloud_provider::aws to each SQS-Based S3 input (the inputs the AWS S3 Direct screen creates get it automatically). The Data TA’s Configuration → Cloud Provider dropdown ships as Not set; see Choose Cloud Attribution for when to change it.

Ingest channel: AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, or Google Cloud Storage

The sourcetype mappings below apply identically to all three ingest channels — AWS S3 (via the Splunk Add-on for AWS), Azure Blob Storage (via the LogServ Azure add-on), and Google Cloud Storage (via the LogServ GCP add-on). The Data TA’s index-time routing transforms key on the clz_dir / clz_subdir fields carried inside each NDJSON event (and, for the Linux, DNS, proxy, Windows and Web Dispatcher access types and for HANA trace files delivered without folder fields, on the event’s source path), which the SAP LogServ collector writes the same way regardless of object-storage destination. AWS S3 setup is covered in Choose Your Cloud and AWS Scenario and its AWS guides; see the Azure Setup Guide and the GCP Setup Guide for the other clouds. Azure- and GCP-ingested events carry an indexed cloud_provider field automatically (stamped per input by their add-on); AWS-ingested events carry it once _meta = cloud_provider::aws is on each AWS S3 input — see Choose Cloud Attribution.

docs.title: LogServ Object Storage Path Structure
docs.text:
The log files in the SAP LogServ object storage location (AWS S3 bucket, Azure Blob Storage container, or GCS bucket) follow this path pattern (the leading container/prefix segment is environment-specific — logserv/ here; some landscapes use e.g. clzlogserv/):

<prefix>/<clz_dir>/<clz_subdir>/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>/<filename>.json.gz

For example:

logserv/linux/messages/2025/09/15/messages-abc123.json.gz
logserv/hana/hanaaudit/2025/10/01/hana-xyz789.json.gz
logserv/dns/binddns/2025/11/20/dns-def456.json.gz

The clz_dir/clz_subdir values are used by the index-time filter to match include/exclude patterns. The filter’s Include Sources and Exclude Sources fields match the event’s source value instead — the log file’s path, such as /var/log/zypper.log — which is how log files that share a folder are told apart. See Configuring Filters for details. Some Azure data sits in a folder named undefined/undefined and its events carry no folder fields; see Data Delivered Without Folder Fields.

docs.title: Primary Supported Log Types
docs.text: These log types have dedicated parsing logic — index-time routing to a specific final sourcetype, plus search-time field extractions — to provide the most accurate parsing. The tables below show the sourcetype mapping for each.

docs.title: SAP HANA Audit (LogServ App)
docs.text:
The LogServ App provides rich search-time field extractions for SAP HANA audit events — the full audit-record field set (service, host, SID, user, action, status, SQL statement, and the derived risk/criticality fields) plus CIM field aliases.

Source field value Sourcetype assigned Filter path hana audit log sap:hana:audit hana/hanaaudit

docs.title: SAP Web Dispatcher (LogServ App)
docs.text:
The LogServ App provides search-time field extractions for SAP Web Dispatcher access logs — client/method/status/URI, four-stage timing, TLS posture, and derived response-time / error fields, plus CIM field aliases. Like the ABAP sourcetypes, it also extracts sap_sid and sap_instance from the source metadata field (/usr/sap/<SID>/<instance>/...): a path with no /usr/sap/<SID>/ directory (three upper-case letters or digits) gets no sap_sid, and one with no instance directory (upper-case letters followed by digits, such as W00) right below /usr/sap/<dir>/ gets no sap_instance.

Source field value Sourcetype assigned Filter path web dispatcher access log sap:webdispatcher:access webdispatcher/accesslog

docs.title: SAP ABAP Application Logs (LogServ App)
docs.text:
The LogServ App provides search-time field extractions for 9 SAP ABAP application log types. Each sourcetype includes sap_sid and sap_instance extraction from the source metadata field, plus type-specific field extractions.

Source field value Sourcetype assigned Filter path ABAP security audit log sap:abap:audit abap/audit ABAP dispatcher log † sap:abap:dispatcher abap/dispatcher ABAP enqueue server log sap:abap:enqueueserver abap/enqueueserver ABAP event log † sap:abap:event abap/event ABAP gateway log sap:abap:gateway abap/gateway ABAP ICM (Internet Communication Manager) log sap:abap:icm abap/icm ABAP message server log sap:abap:messageserver abap/messageserver ABAP sapstartsrv log sap:abap:sapstartsrv abap/sapstartsrv ABAP work process log † sap:abap:workprocess abap/workprocess

The ICM log (dev_icm) gives the request type, session ID, SAP client (sap_client), user and terminal of each session-list entry, the direction, addresses and protocol of each connection, and the class of the ICM’s own messages (icm_severity: ERROR or WARNING). It records no HTTP status code. The Data TA gives this sourcetype to the abap/icm folder only. Data TA builds up to 1791935359 (2026-10-13) gave it to every LogServ folder named icm, so a Web Dispatcher’s own ICM log (webdispatcher/icm) indexed by them is sap:abap:icm, with the Web Dispatcher’s sap_sid and sap_instance; from build 1792189743 (2026-10-16) it keeps sap_logserv_logs, like the Web Dispatcher’s other secondary folders.

† Discontinued from LogServ scope — effective April 2026

SAP discontinued three of the ABAP log types above from LogServ delivery effective April 2026:

  • ABAP work process log — sap:abap:workprocess
  • ABAP dispatcher log — sap:abap:dispatcher
  • ABAP event log (external events) — sap:abap:event

LogServ no longer delivers new events for these sourcetypes. The LogServ App retains their parsing logic and dashboards, and any data already ingested remains fully searchable — but no new events will arrive through LogServ going forward.

SAP also discontinued the ABAP transport log (abap/transport, /usr/sap/trans/log) in the same April 2026 change; LogServ never routed it to a dedicated sourcetype, so it does not appear in the tables on this page.

If you require continued collection of these logs, please contact SAP directly to discuss the options available for your environment.

docs.title: SAP HANA Trace Logs (LogServ App)
docs.text:
The LogServ App provides search-time field extractions for HANA trace logs, including SID/instance extraction from the source path.

Source field value Sourcetype assigned Filter path HANA trace log sap:hana:tracelogs hana/tracelogs HANA trace log delivered without folder fields: a .trc file or backup.log in /usr/sap/<SID>/HDB<nn>/<host>/trace/ or its DB_<tenant>/ subfolder sap:hana:tracelogs none — Include Sources or Exclude Sources /usr/sap/*/HDB??/*/trace/*

Real Azure deliveries can send the HANA trace directory without clz_dir and clz_subdir (see Data Delivered Without Folder Fields); on the reference system all of the real HANA trace data arrived that way. The Data TA routes these events by their source path instead, and only when the event has no folder fields; an event that has them is routed by its folder as before. Other files in the trace directory, such as backint.log or compressed .trc.gz files, and files in deeper subfolders keep the base sap_logserv_logs sourcetype, and so do HANA trace events indexed by an earlier Data TA build. Routing does not add folder fields, so a folder pattern such as hana/tracelogs never matches these files: in Include Filters it does not keep them (an allow-list drops them), and in Exclude Filters it does not drop them. Use the source pattern in the table.

docs.title: SAP Cloud Connector (LogServ App)
docs.text:
The LogServ App provides search-time field extractions for SAP Cloud Connector audit and HTTP access logs.

Source field value Sourcetype assigned Filter path SCC audit log (CSV format) sap:scc:audit scc/audit SCC HTTP access log sap:scc:http_access scc/tracelogs

docs.title: SAP Service Logs (LogServ App)
docs.text:
The LogServ App provides search-time field extractions for SAP host-level service logs. These are infrastructure services that run at the host control level (/usr/sap/hostctrl/) rather than within a specific SAP instance.

Source field value Sourcetype assigned Filter path SAP Start Service log (auth, SSL/TLS) sap:sapstartsrv sap/sapstartsrv SAP Host Agent execution log sap:saphostexec sap/saphostexec SAP Router connection and trace log sap:saprouter sap/saprouter

SAP Service Log Details

  • sap:sapstartsrv includes fields for OS authentication failures, SSL/TLS negotiation errors (protocol version, cipher suite, peer addresses), and webmethod invocation failures.
  • sap:saprouter covers both .log files (CONNECT/DISCONNECT/INVAL DATA events with connection IDs and host addresses) and .trc files (NiBuf/NiI error traces with peer/local addresses and return codes) as a single sourcetype.
  • On GCP the router’s records can also arrive as /var/log/messages lines in the sap/saprouter folder. These lines get sap:saprouter too. On the reference system at least 70% of them, in the one hour measured, were the router’s own connection and trace records, and the rest the router container’s wrapper output and other text; every line had the same tagged syslog form, and the newest lines carry the router container’s tag. They are router data, so do not drop them with an entry such as sap/saprouter=/var/log/messages.

docs.title: Linux OS logs
docs.text:
The LogServ App parses linux:cron, linux:warn, linux:sudolog, linux:slapd, lastlog, who and linux_messages_syslog itself; the first four are LogServ-App-owned names, deliberately distinct from the pretrained names of the Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux. The App ships no extraction for linux_secure: its firewall and kernel panels parse those events inline, and their CIM fields come from the Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux on the search tier.

Source field value Sourcetype assigned Filter path /lastlog lastlog linux/linux_secure /var/log/cron linux:cron linux/cron /var/log/firewall linux_secure linux/linux_secure /var/log/kernel linux_secure linux/linux_secure /var/log/localmessages linux_messages_syslog linux/localmessages /var/log/messages linux_messages_syslog linux/messages, linux/proxy /var/log/pacemaker/pacemaker.log linux:slapd linux/pacemaker, linux/slapd /var/log/slapd.log linux:slapd linux/slapd /var/log/sssd/sssd* linux_secure linux/linux_secure /var/log/sudolog linux:sudolog linux/sudolog /var/log/warn linux:warn linux/warn /who who linux/linux_secure

On /var/log/pacemaker/pacemaker.log lines the App extracts resource_agent and cluster_resource from resource-agent lines and pacemaker_daemon and pacemaker_function from daemon lines. slapd.log lines name no user.

docs.title: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows
docs.text:
Source field value Sourcetype assigned Filter path WinEventLog:Application XmlWinEventLog windows/WinEventLog:Application WinEventLog:(*.)Operational XmlWinEventLog windows/WinEventLog:Powershell WinEventLog:Security XmlWinEventLog windows/WinEventLog:Security WinEventLog:System XmlWinEventLog windows/WinEventLog:System

The LogServ App ships no XmlWinEventLog extraction: fields such as EventCode, severity and signature come from the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742) on the search head.

docs.title: Squid Proxy (squid:access, squid:cache, squid:store)
docs.text:
Parsing of Squid’s native format is absorbed into the LogServ App (from the archived Splunk Add-on for Squid Proxy v2.1.0 — no longer required as a separate install), and the App parses the logformat=splunk_recommended_squid key=value format SAP LogServ proxy logs use with its own transforms. Each file has its own sourcetype: access.log holds the requests, cache.log the daemon’s own messages and store.log the object-store journal. Data indexed by an earlier Data TA carries all three as squid:access, so the dashboards count only access.log lines as requests.

Source field value Sourcetype assigned Filter path /var/log/squid/access.log squid:access proxy/squid, linux/proxy /var/log/squid/cache.log squid:cache proxy/squid, linux/proxy /var/log/squid/store.log squid:store proxy/squid, linux/proxy

Real LogServ deliveries do not all use one folder layout. The AWS bucket files Squid under proxy/squid; Azure delivers it under linux/proxy; GCP delivers pacemaker.log under linux/pacemaker and a proxy VM’s /var/log/messages under linux/proxy. The Filter path columns list every path seen, and the Data TA declares all of them, so a filter rule meant to cover a log type on every cloud names each of its paths — proxy/squid, linux/proxy for Squid. To exclude Squid, keep in mind that linux/proxy also carries a proxy VM’s /var/log/messages: Exclude Filters proxy/squid with Exclude Sources linux/proxy=/var/log/squid/* drops the Squid files of both layouts and keeps those lines.

docs.title: ISC BIND (isc:bind:*)
docs.text:
Parsing is absorbed natively into the LogServ App (from the archived Splunk Add-on for ISC BIND v2.0.0 — no longer required as a separate install).

Source field value Sourcetype assigned Filter path /var/lib/named/log/named/default.log isc:bind:query dns/binddns /var/lib/named/log/named/general.log isc:bind:network dns/binddns /var/lib/named/log/named/lame-servers.log isc:bind:lameserver dns/binddns /var/lib/named/log/named/network.log isc:bind:network dns/binddns /var/lib/named/log/named/notify.log isc:bind:transfer dns/binddns /var/lib/named/log/named/queries.log isc:bind:query dns/binddns /var/lib/named/log/named/resolver.log isc:bind:network dns/binddns /var/lib/named/log/named/update.log isc:bind:transfer dns/binddns /var/lib/named/log/named/xfer-out.log isc:bind:transfer dns/binddns

Filter Path Column

The Filter path column shows the clz_dir/clz_subdir value used in the index-time filter include/exclude patterns. See Configuring Filters for details.

Source Field Value Column

In the Linux, Windows, Squid and ISC BIND tables the Source field value column shows the source values that the filter’s Include Sources and Exclude Sources fields match; the SAP tables describe the log instead. Some rows are shorthand rather than literal values: /var/log/sssd/sssd* stands for every sssd file, rotated copies such as /var/log/sssd/sssd.log-20260913 included, and WinEventLog:(*.)Operational for the Operational channels. Real deliveries on the reference system carry lastlog and who without the leading / that the table shows (the routing accepts both forms). A source pattern must match the whole value and is case-sensitive, so list the values your own deliveries carry before writing one — see Source Pattern Syntax.

docs.title: Secondary Supported Log Types
docs.text:
The log types below are within LogServ’s scope and are ingested and fully searchable once SAP has activated them for your landscape (Network and WAF/F5 logs are activated only on request, and WAF/F5 applies only if your RISE package includes WAF or F5), but they do not have the dedicated index-time routing and search-time field extractions that the Primary types above have. They remain under the base sap_logserv_logs sourcetype in raw form; detailed, per-type parsing may be added in a future release.

These data sources are drawn from Section 2 (“Data sources”) of the SAP LogServ service description and are the sources not covered by a Primary parser above. Each entry ends with how to keep it out of the index with the Data TA’s filters (Configuration → Filters, Enable Filtering checked; see Configuring Filters for complete recipes).

  • Network / Flow logs — VPC/VNET network-traffic flow logs (source/destination IPs, ports, protocols, and traffic statistics). Category-level in the source document; no dedicated clz_dir/clz_subdir; activated on request. Filter: the folder is not known, so only an Include Filters allow-list drops it; once you know its folder or source values, name them in Exclude Filters or Exclude Sources.
  • WAF / F5 logs — Web Application Firewall / F5 traffic and firewall system events (successful and failed connection attempts). Category-level; no dedicated clz_dir/clz_subdir; activated on request. Filter: as for Network / Flow — an Include Filters allow-list, or an exclude once the folder or source is known.
  • SAP ABAP — transport + HTTP access — the ABAP transport log (abap/transport — discontinued by SAP from LogServ scope effective April 2026) and the ABAP HTTP access log (abap/httpaccess, newly added to LogServ scope). Filter: Exclude Filters abap/transport, abap/httpaccess; an allow-list must name the Primary ABAP folders one by one, since abap/* keeps both.
  • SAP Web Dispatcher — process / sapstartsrv / dev_icm traces — webdispatcher/process, webdispatcher/sapstartsrv, webdispatcher/devicm; only webdispatcher/accesslog has a Primary parser. The Web Dispatcher’s ICM log (webdispatcher/icm) is raw as well; Data TA builds up to 1791935359 (2026-10-13) typed it sap:abap:icm (see the ICM paragraph above). Filter: Exclude Filters webdispatcher/process, webdispatcher/icm, webdispatcher/sapstartsrv, webdispatcher/devicm, or webdispatcher/accesslog (not webdispatcher/*) in an allow-list.
  • Additional Linux system logs — /var/log/zypper.log, /var/log/YaST2 (linux/linux_secure), and /var/log/cluster/corosync.log (linux/pacemaker). Filter: these share their folders with Primary log types — linux/linux_secure also holds the firewall, kernel, sssd, lastlog and who logs, and linux/pacemaker the Pacemaker cluster log — so a folder pattern cannot drop them without dropping those too. Drop them by source with Exclude Sources: /var/log/zypper.log*, /var/log/YaST2/* for zypper and YaST2 (real deliveries carry /var/log/zypper.log, /var/log/YaST2/mkinitrd.log and /var/log/YaST2/config_diff_<date>.log), and /var/log/cluster/corosync.log* for corosync. corosync.log has not been observed in real data on the reference system; the path is the one the service description names, so confirm the source value your deliveries carry before relying on the pattern. See Recipe 3.
  • Database — SAP ASE (Sybase) — ASE error log, Backup Server log, and Job scheduler error log (sybase/install). Filter: Exclude Filters sybase/*.
  • Database — Microsoft SQL Server — MSSQL database audit logs (MSSQLDBAudit). Filter: no folder is known, so only an Include Filters allow-list drops them; once you know their folder or source values, exclude those.
  • SAP NetWeaver Java — deploy, JSMON, JStart, server, ICM, security, and general trace/log files (java/*). Filter: Exclude Filters java/*.
  • SAP BusinessObjects (BOBJ — BI / BODS / IPS) — BI/IPS, BODS and Jobserver, Webapp, Tomcat, and SAC Agent logs (bobj_bi/*, bobj_bods/*, bobj_sacagent/*). Filter: Exclude Filters bobj_bi/*, bobj_bods/*, bobj_sacagent/*.
  • DP Agent (Data Provisioning Agent) — framework alert and trace logs (dpagent/alert, dpagent/trace). Filter: Exclude Filters dpagent/*.

Check the folders and files your own deliveries use

The folder names above come from the service description; none of these Secondary folders has appeared in the reference system’s real deliveries, while the zypper and YaST2 files have. Before relying on a rule, list what your deliveries carry under the base sourcetype:

| tstats count where `sap_logserv_idx_macro` sourcetype=sap_logserv_logs by clz_dir, clz_subdir, source

Some events carry no folder fields at all and do not appear in that list — see Data Delivered Without Folder Fields below. An Include Filters allow-list drops them unless Include Sources keeps them.

Out of scope

Per the LogServ service description, DB2 and MaxDB database logs are not in LogServ scope, and are therefore not listed above.

docs.title: Data Delivered Without Folder Fields
docs.text:
SAP files some Azure data in a storage folder named undefined/undefined (<prefix>/undefined/undefined/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>/), and its events carry no clz_dir or clz_subdir. In about four weeks of real Azure deliveries on the reference system it was about 19.9 million events of two kinds, each from a single host:

  • Unix command output — about 19.4 million events, with source values ps, netstat, iostat, cpu, nfsiostat, top, openPorts, interfaces, df, bandwidth, vmstat and Unix:ListeningPorts; ps alone is about 80%. Together that is about 0.7 million events and roughly 125 MB of text a day. This output is not among the data sources the LogServ service description lists. They stay under the base sap_logserv_logs sourcetype and are not parsed: each event holds one table row, a header line on its own, or a table whose line breaks are written as the two characters \n.
  • HANA trace files — about 566,000 events, the .trc files and backup.log of /usr/sap/<SID>/HDB<nn>/<host>/trace/. The Data TA routes them to sap:hana:tracelogs by their source path (see SAP HANA Trace Logs).

Folder patterns cannot reach either kind: an Include Filters allow-list drops them all, hana/tracelogs in Include Filters does not keep the trace files, and no Exclude Filters entry drops them. Use Include Sources and Exclude Sources, which match the source value.

Drop the Unix command output unless you need it

If you do not use this output, drop it with Exclude Sources ps, top, netstat, iostat, vmstat, df, cpu, interfaces, bandwidth, openPorts, nfsiostat, Unix:ListeningPorts. If you keep it, review who can search it: a ps row can carry the arguments a process was started with — up to 34% of the real ps rows checked on the reference system did — and process arguments can contain passwords, keys or tokens. See Configuring Filters → Events Without Folder Fields.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This page lists common symptoms and the section that explains each one. If you are not sure the data arrives at all, start with Verify Your Data; if a dashboard panel is empty, start with the LogServ App’s Data Doctor.

docs.title: Data Arrival and Parsing
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause Where to look No events in sap_logserv_logs The input cannot read: credentials, SAP’s policies or grants, the network path, or a wrong queue or subscription name Verify Your Data → Per-Forwarder Checks; your AWS guide’s last step (Connect, Filter, Copy); Azure troubleshooting; GCP troubleshooting Events keep the sourcetype sap_logserv_logs, have no folder fields and no splunk_solution The Data TA was not on the instance that parsed them, or the input started before the Data TA reached it. Those events stay as they were indexed Verify Your Data, check 1; Version Check; Distribute the Data TA Events arrive under another sourcetype, with no folder fields and no splunk_solution The AWS SQS-Based S3 input’s Source Type is not sap_logserv_logs, so the Data TA’s rules do not run on its events. Events already indexed stay as they are Your AWS guide’s SQS-Based S3 input step: Connect, Filter, Copy; Verify Your Data, check 1 A folder the Data TA routes by folder alone (for example hana/hanaaudit) stays under sap_logserv_logs The routes did not run as shipped on the forwarder that parsed it: check its Data TA build, and look for a local/ override of the routes Verify Your Data, check 4; Version Check Most Azure data stays under sap_logserv_logs The Unix command output SAP delivers without folder fields stays there by design Data Delivered Without Folder Fields; Configuring Filters → Events Without Folder Fields Events arrive hours or days late after the first start, and the forwarder is busy SAP’s queue backlog is draining First Start: The Queue Backlog; Measure Your Own Heavy Forwarder An Azure or GCP event is indexed twice More than one input reads the same queue or subscription Multiple landscapes / fleets: Azure, GCP A search that uses sap_logserv_idx_macro fails on the search head (the macro cannot be found) Neither the Data TA nor the LogServ App is on that search head yet Verify Your Data has the same checks with the index name

docs.title: Cloud Attribution
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause Where to look cloud_provider is missing in your own searches or in tstats An AWS SQS-Based S3 input without _meta = cloud_provider::aws, or the stamp was set up after the events were indexed. The LogServ App’s dashboards count such events as aws; other searches do not Choose Cloud Attribution; Verify Your Data, check 2 mvcount(cloud_provider) is 2 The Data TA’s Cloud Provider dropdown is set while the input stamps its own value: an Azure or GCP input with the dropdown on any value, or an AWS S3 Direct backfill with the dropdown on AWS. A dropdown value different from the input’s is seen in the lab; the same-value case follows from how Splunk writes _meta and has not been reproduced Choose Cloud Attribution → What Gets Stamped; Check the Result

docs.title: Azure and GCP Inputs
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause Where to look Azure input log: queue read failed (... 403 ...) The SAS lacks queue process (p), ss lacks q, srt lacks o, or the SAS has expired Azure troubleshooting; What the SAP-provided SAS must cover The input worked for weeks, then its log shows 403 or forbidden errors The Azure SAS has passed its expiry (se=), or the GCP service-account key was disabled or deleted Rotate credentials: Azure, GCP; Azure troubleshooting; GCP troubleshooting Saving an Azure or GCP input fails with 403 “This operation is forbidden” Your role lacks admin_all_objects, which creating, editing and deleting an input need Splunk Cloud Considerations → Capability-gated REST endpoints; configure the input: Azure, GCP The input logs done: messages=0 at every firing, but objects exist SAP’s notification is not reaching the queue or subscription, or its name is wrong Azure troubleshooting; GCP troubleshooting

docs.title: AWS
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause Where to look The Filter scenario’s Lambda logs Could not retrieve S3 object, discarding message, Failed to forward message to target SQS, discarding or Unexpected error processing message The Lambda deleted SAP’s notification without forwarding it, so that object was not ingested AWS Remote S3 Filter, step 10; after fixing the cause, load the missing days with AWS S3 Direct The AWS S3 Direct screen shows “Apply this as an administrator” instead of a Create backfill button Your account lacks admin_all_objects (or the screen could not confirm your capabilities), a read of the Splunk Add-on for AWS configuration that a create needs failed, or a Deployment Server manages the Splunk Add-on for AWS on this instance. The screen names the reason AWS S3 Direct → Troubleshooting; The AWS S3 Direct screen; Splunk Cloud Considerations An AWS S3 Direct backfill gets AccessDenied, finds nothing, or skips days s3:ListBucket missing (for SAP’s bucket, also in SAP’s bucket policy), days already covered or filtered out, and the other causes in its table AWS S3 Direct → Troubleshooting Backfilled events can be searched at first, then disappear The index’s retention is shorter than the age of the days you loaded: Splunk freezes a bucket once its newest event is older than the retention Raise the retention of sap_logserv_logs (Create the Indexes), then load those days again; AWS S3 Direct → Troubleshooting A step of the migration from AWS Remote S3 Connect to Filter fails See the migration guide Connect to Filter migration → Troubleshooting

docs.title: Upgrading to This Release
docs.text:
Use this page to bring an existing Splunk for SAP LogServ installation up to the current release: LogServ App build 394, Data TA build 1792598960, LogServ Azure add-on build 1792558069 and LogServ GCP add-on build 1792558072, all at version 0.1.2. It applies whether you come from 0.0.5, 0.0.6, 0.1.1 or an earlier 0.1.2 build: find your builds, note the rows of the work list that apply to them, then follow the upgrade sequence.

What an upgrade does not touch

No data is re-ingested. Events already indexed keep the sourcetype, host, source and folder fields they were indexed with: the Data TA’s routing changes apply only to events parsed after you update it. The local/ configuration of every package and the App’s KV Store data (settings, acknowledgements, saved layouts, dashboard data) survive the upgrade. Two things do change for data you already have: some search-time fields, which every search computes anew, and the values some dashboard rollups store, which is why some rows in Settings → Dashboard Data need a one-time rebuild.

docs.title: 1. Find Your Builds
docs.text:
LogServ App. Click About at the bottom of the App’s left navigation rail. The dialog shows the version, the build and the build date. (App builds 302 to 338 have About in the top navigation bar; earlier builds have none.) On any build, the same from a search on the search head:

| rest /services/apps/local splunk_server=local
| search title=splunk_app_sap_logserv
| table title version build

Data TA. Check each instance that parses LogServ data, every heavy forwarder or the single instance, not only the Deployment Server: see Version Check. Every 0.1.2 Data TA build has the version 0.1.2; the builds are told apart only by their build number, which is the time the package was built, in epoch seconds.

LogServ Azure and GCP add-ons. Run the search above on each heavy forwarder, or search head, that runs them, with title=splunk_ta_sap_logserv_azure or title=splunk_ta_sap_logserv_gcp.

Then read your App build in the work list’s terms:

Your LogServ App Use in the work list Version 0.1.2 Its build number Version 0.1.1, build 282 to 335, or version 0.0.6, build 258 or later (266 is its last build, and carries the 0.1.1 changes up to build 299) Build 335 Version 0.1.1, build 245 to 281, or version 0.0.6 before build 258 Build 281: a full rebuild of the dashboard data Version 0.0.5, or version 0.1.1, build 244 or earlier Build 244: a pre-rollup build

docs.title: 2. The Work List
docs.text: Each row of the tables below starts at the last build that lacks a change. Apply every row whose build is at or above yours, all of them, in one pass after the upgrade. Rows about Settings → Dashboard Data say which rows there to rebuild; How to Rebuild a Row gives the steps.

docs.title: Rows to Rebuild, by Starting Build
docs.text:
The Dashboard Data steps of the App work list, combined for the builds an upgrade usually starts from. A row that one change clears and another only backfills needs its Clear and Backfill once. The rows are named as in Settings → Dashboard Data; Beaconing detection there reads Beaconing detection (Environment Health / DNS / Network Perimeter).

Your App build Clear, then Backfill Backfill only, without Clear 383 or later None None 379 Work Process Performance / ABAP Operations None 378 Work Process Performance / ABAP Operations Host Role Activity (Host Details); Environment Topology (graph) 364 to 377 12 rows: Work Process Performance / ABAP Operations; HANA Audit; HANA Trace; Environment Health; ABAP Network & Security; Host Role Activity (Host Details); Environment Topology (graph); Environment Topology (detail tabs); Multi-Cloud Overview; Data Pipeline Overview; Host Details; Sourcetype Mapping (Host Details / Data Pipeline) Change & Configuration Activity; Cross-Stack Authentication 358 to 363 (the released builds 360, 362 and 363) 14 rows: the 12 above, Proxy Analytics and Cross-Stack Authentication Change & Configuration Activity; Network Perimeter; Beaconing detection 355 or earlier: 336 (the first 0.1.2 build), or 335 (from the table above) 17 rows: the 14 above, Beaconing detection, Change & Configuration Activity and Linux System & Security / Network Perimeter Network Perimeter 281 (from the table above) Every row, with Clear all data None 244 (from the table above) Every row, with Clear all data: the rollups start empty, but the Environment Topology (graph) row already holds the earlier build’s rows None

The other steps of the work list still apply to you, whichever line of this table you are on.

docs.title: LogServ App
docs.text:
Coming from App build 388 or later, there is nothing to rebuild, and no acknowledgement is asked again.

Coming from App build Changed in After upgrading 386 or earlier 388 With the AI Assistant enabled, the next admin who clicks Save Defaults in Settings → AI Assistant → General is asked once to accept the enablement acknowledgement, now at version 3; answering No turns the AI Assistant off. While it is disabled nothing is asked, until it is turned on, which always asks. A local/ai_assistant_acks.conf that sets optInVersion under [logserv-ai-assistant-enable-tc] keeps the old version: remove that line. See Legal Acknowledgement Modals. 385 or earlier 386 With audit forwarding off, the next Save Defaults asks once to acknowledge the audit-log integrity text, now at version 2. With forwarding on nothing is asked. An optInVersion line under [logserv-ai-assistant-tc] in local/ai_assistant_acks.conf keeps the old version: remove it. 383 or earlier 385 The App’s collections that hold dashboard data (the rollups, the five Environment Topology data collections and the Data Doctor’s platform snapshot) can be written by the admin, sc_admin and sc_subadmin roles only; every role still reads them. The topology layout collections (saved layouts, their defaults and each user’s layout mode), the dashboard refresh intervals and the Data Doctor’s saved reports and ingest facts stay writable by every role. The App’s scheduled searches and the Settings backfill keep working. Its searches that write these collections run as the user who starts them. A [collections/<name>] stanza with an access line in the App’s metadata/local.meta keeps its own permissions: remove it to take the new ones. A scheduled search of your own that writes into one of these collections and is owned by a non-admin user stops writing. Start the App’s writing searches (a retention, a backfill, an ES feed) through the REST API only with an admin-tier account. 379 or earlier 383, the first released build after 379 Clear, then Backfill Work Process Performance / ABAP Operations, or use the narrower repair. wp_category_name takes SAP’s names for the work process trace components: ten values are renamed and nine more letters get names (field changes). The AI Assistant’s settings, acknowledgements and model cache can be written by admin-tier roles only. Users whose roles hold neither edit_tcp nor edit_log_alert_event now see a warning in the AI Assistant panel: their AI Assistant activity is not written to the audit index (Who Can Write Audit Events). 378 or earlier 379 Backfill, without Clear, Host Role Activity (Host Details) and Environment Topology (graph). Where the next row applies too, its Clear and Backfill cover both. 377 or earlier 378 Clear, then Backfill eleven rows and Backfill two more: see Coming From App Build 377 or Earlier. HANA audit, HANA trace and ICM fields change (field changes). 376 or earlier 377 Nothing to rebuild. A search override in local/savedsearches.conf for logserv_topology_aggregate_nodes, logserv_topology_aggregate_edges, logserv_topology_detail_aggregate, logserv_topology_enrichment_aggregate or one of their backfill twins keeps the old loopback filter, which leaves out only 127.0.0.1: remove it to take the shipped search, which leaves out every loopback address (127.0.0.0/8). Claude 5.x turns now count toward the AI Assistant’s daily spend cap (daily_spend_cap_usd, Settings → AI Assistant → General): raise it if your users run those models heavily. 375 or earlier 376 Before upgrading, export the threat-intel lists you keep by hand (step 1 of the upgrade sequence). After upgrading, if ES reads the asset and identity feed CSVs and your upgrade method does not keep the App’s lookups/ directory, dispatch both feeds once (Customer Wire-up). A search override of logserv_topology_retention in local/savedsearches.conf keeps the old search, which trims the edges inside a subsearch of the nodes trim: remove it. The nightly retention window now ends at 02:36. 374 or earlier 375 Earlier builds could empty a rollup when Splunkd restarted just before the nightly retention. In Settings → Dashboard Data, a row whose aggregation is on but whose History reads empty, or much shorter than you expect, can be rebuilt with Backfill over the history you want, as far back as its raw events are still in the index (at most 365 days). A search override for a logserv_*_retention stanza in local/savedsearches.conf keeps the old behaviour: remove it, or add override_if_empty=false to each outputlookup it runs. 366 or earlier 367 Nothing to rebuild. vendor_product and app on linux:slapd change for Pacemaker lines (field changes). 363 or earlier 364 to 365 Clear, then Backfill Proxy Analytics, HANA Audit and Cross-Stack Authentication; then Backfill, without Clear, Network Perimeter, Environment Health, Beaconing detection and the two Environment Topology rows, which recount what they hold. Rows written before keep the old values, some under the old key (none). Proxy request totals fall where Squid’s store.log and cache.log are collected: those lines are not requests and are no longer counted. Several fields change (field changes). 357 or earlier 356 to 358 Clear, then Backfill Linux System & Security / Network Perimeter: it recorded fragments of ordinary words as Kernel Event Types. Coming from 356 or earlier, also Change & Configuration Activity: it stored the after-hours flag in the time zone of the search that wrote the row, so where a Settings backfill ran in another time zone than the search head’s, hours were stored twice. Coming from 355 or earlier, also Beaconing detection: it keyed each day on midnight in the writing search’s time zone, so a day could be stored twice. Each rebuild is safe whether or not your data was affected. 281 or earlier 282 The dashboard rollups (all but the Environment Topology’s) added cloud_provider to the keys of their rows. Clear all data (Settings → Dashboard Data, Danger zone), then Run backfill over the history you want. This replaces every other Clear and Backfill of this list. 244 or earlier 245 The dashboards move to the rollup collections, which the upgrade creates empty; the Environment Topology collections already hold the earlier build’s rows: see Coming From a Pre-rollup Build. Clear all data (Settings → Dashboard Data, Danger zone), then one Run backfill over the history you want. This replaces every other Clear and Backfill of this list.

docs.title: Coming From App Build 377 or Earlier
docs.text:
App build 378 changes values that several rollups store, most of them in the keys the rows are stored under:

  • the search-time host of HANA audit events is the HANA host that wrote the record (the client’s host name is src_host), and HANA audit records with no client fields now parse;
  • HANA trace lines take severity, component and duration from their exact format (backup.log levels; hdbcons timings in microseconds and seconds converted to milliseconds; hdbcons, SQL-trace, load and availability files carry no severity);
  • RFC edges in the Environment Topology count connections, in the direction they were made;
  • the three digits after a session ID in the ICM trace (dev_icm) are read as the SAP client (sap_client), no longer as an HTTP status, so the ICM error counts change and the ICM status panels are replaced.

Rows written earlier keep the old values, most under the old keys. The first hourly run after the upgrade rewrites the last hour or two under the new keys, so those hours count twice until rebuilt, and so does any later Backfill over earlier days, Backfill N days for late-arriving data included. Until you rebuild: HANA Audit’s Failed Operations by HANA Host lists client hosts beside the HANA hosts for the days before the upgrade; HANA Trace keeps record files under UNKNOWN and backup.log lines under fragment components, and misses microsecond-timed commands; ABAP Network & Security counts ICM sessions in SAP clients 400 to 599 as ICM errors; the Environment Topology draws a second, reversed edge for the old RFC rows, and an edge with a node of its own for each client host name of the old HANA audit rows. After the upgrade, the average on HANA Trace’s hdbcons Command Duration (Avg / Max) panel usually falls, because microsecond-timed commands now count.

After the upgrade (a Clear before it is undone by the old build’s last runs), Clear, then Backfill each of these rows with a window that covers its whole history, using each row’s own Backfill:

  • HANA Audit
  • HANA Trace
  • Environment Health
  • ABAP Network & Security
  • Host Role Activity (Host Details)
  • Environment Topology (graph)
  • Environment Topology (detail tabs)
  • Multi-Cloud Overview
  • Data Pipeline Overview
  • Host Details
  • Sourcetype Mapping (Host Details / Data Pipeline)

Then Backfill, without Clear, Change & Configuration Activity and Cross-Stack Authentication: they gain the HANA audit records that have no client fields, under keys that do not change.

  • A Backfill without the Clear counts the upgraded hours twice, on Environment Health too, which sums its error counts across hosts. On ABAP Network & Security alone it keeps the old ICM error counts instead. Where the search below returns 0, your ICM error counts were never affected, and a Backfill alone is enough on that row:

    | inputlookup logserv_abapnet_rollup where metric="icmerr" | stats count

  • Keep the Settings page open until the Environment Topology (graph) row has finished: that row writes each month only once every search of the month has finished. SAP Router edges have no history until the Environment Topology rows are backfilled.

  • The Clear removes everything a row holds, including history older than the raw events still in your index, which no Backfill can bring back. To keep that history, use the narrower repair instead.
  • This rebuild also re-keys the RFC rows by application server, the change of 0.1.1 builds 324 to 325. No separate RFC migration is needed: do not run the RFC-only steps in the 0.1.1 release notes on this release. The shipped edges backfill now has two gateway searches, one per direction, and those steps keep only one of them.
  • A search override in local/savedsearches.conf for a rollup aggregation or backfill search keeps the old search after the upgrade: compare it with the shipped one, or remove it.
  • sap:abap:icm leaves the CIM Web data model (its sap_abap_icm_request eventtype is removed). If that data model is accelerated, ICM events summarized before the upgrade stay in its summaries until they age out of the summary range or you rebuild the acceleration.
  • With a Data TA build before 1792189743, the AWS S3 Direct screen does not list the sap/saprouter folder under the two Environment Topology rows: when you load SAP Router history from S3 for the topology, also select its SAP Router row.

docs.title: Coming From a Pre-rollup Build
docs.text:
Current dashboards read most panels from KV Store rollup collections. On the first upgrade from a pre-rollup build (0.0.5, or a 0.1.1 build 244 or earlier) the rollup collections are created empty, and the rolled-up panels show no data until they fill. The Environment Topology collections are not empty: the earlier build already kept and filled them, with RFC edges keyed before the per-application-server breakdown and drawn in the opposite direction, and HANA audit edges to client hosts. A Backfill does not remove those rows, and the topology keeps them for up to 365 days beside the new ones, so the Environment Topology would draw doubled or reversed RFC edges and nodes for client hosts.

  1. Clear all data first: in Settings → Dashboard Data, Danger zone, after the upgrade and clear of the nightly retention window. It empties every rollup and the Environment Topology collections; the rollups are empty anyway.
  2. Run the backfill once (recommended on any install with real data): choose a Backfill window that covers the raw history your index holds, usually the 365-day preset, then click Run backfill. The window is 30 days by default; it also offers 60, 90, 180 or 365 days, or a custom range of whole UTC days back to the 365-day retention. The backfill is idempotent and can be run again. See Backfilling on First Install. Without it, the hourly aggregation searches fill the collections one hour at a time from the upgrade on.

The tstats panels (Data Pipeline Overview, the Host Details counts, Multi-Cloud Overview and the count KPIs) read the index directly and work at once, and so does every panel at a time range under 90 minutes, which reads raw events.

Coming from a 0.0.5 build before 192 or a 0.1.1 build before 240, open the App once as an admin after the upgrade: on that first page load it copies the AI Assistant settings and acknowledgements that those builds kept in local/ conf files into the KV Store.

docs.title: New Scheduled Searches, New Collections, and a Restart
docs.text: Relative to a pre-rollup build, the upgrade adds the rollup aggregation, retention and detection searches and the rollup collections. A Splunkd restart is required for the collections to be created and the new searches to register; Splunk Web’s Install app from file upgrade asks for it. The scheduled searches are staggered so the scheduler never bursts; see Scheduled-Search Schedule.

docs.title: Visible UI / Panel Changes When Coming From v0.0.5-era Builds
docs.text:
• Every chart and table panel header has a toolbar (Open in Search, Download CSV, Inspect, Refresh), a loading spinner and the Data Doctor’s Diagnose action; empty panels explain themselves (Data Doctor).
  • Percentile charts (p50 / p95 / p99) become Avg + Max by hour; HANA Trace’s slowest-operations panel is a top-by-max table; Web Dispatcher’s Top URIs has no Unique Clients column.
  • Rolled-up panels are hourly-fresh at wide time ranges; ranges under 90 minutes use the panels’ raw searches, so short-range investigation stays real-time.
  • The App uses the Cisco Magnetic theme (dark by default, with a light mode), a left navigation rail, and the current Environment Topology layout and node designs.
  • Your browser may briefly serve a cached bundle; a hard refresh loads the new build.

docs.title: Search-Time Field Changes
docs.text:
The App computes these fields when a search runs, so the change applies to events old and new as soon as the App is upgraded. The App’s dashboards use the new fields. Saved searches, alerts and reports of your own that read them need the new names or values.

Coming from App build Sourcetype Change 379 or earlier sap:abap:workprocess wp_category_name takes SAP’s names for the trace components: C, D, M, N, O, Q, R, S, T and X are renamed (for example C = Database (DBSL), D = Diag Processor, Q = Other), and E, G, H, I, J, L, P, V and W, which read <letter> = Other, get names. 377 or earlier sap:hana:audit host is the HANA host that wrote the record; the client’s host name is the new src_host. Searches that group by host now group by HANA host. Records with no client fields parse fully. 377 or earlier sap:hana:tracelogs Record files (hdbcons, SQL trace, loads, system availability) carry no hana_trace_severity; backup.log lines carry their own level and component. New fields: hana_trace_file_type, hana_backup_level, hana_op, hana_op_duration, hana_op_duration_unit; hana_op_duration_ms is always in milliseconds. 377 or earlier sap:abap:icm icm_status_code, status and action are gone. The SAP client of a session is sap_client, its user icm_user, its terminal icm_terminal. icm_is_error is true only on lines the ICM logged as errors. On connection lines src and dest follow the connection’s direction (icm_conn_role). The sap_abap_icm_request eventtype and its tag are removed. 377 or earlier sap:webdispatcher:access New sap_sid and sap_instance, read from the log’s path. 377 or earlier sap:saprouter, sap:abap:gateway New fields for the SAP Router targets (saprouter_target_*, saprouter_fail_target_ip) and the gateway’s connection records (gw_remgw_*, gw_client_*, rfc_peer_port, rfc_local_port). 366 or earlier linux:slapd vendor_product and app read Pacemaker and pacemaker on pacemaker.log lines; slapd.log lines keep OpenLDAP and slapd. 364 or earlier linux:slapd os_user is removed. Pacemaker lines carry resource_agent and cluster_resource, or pacemaker_daemon and pacemaker_function. 364 or earlier sap:hana:audit sql_statement and command are shown without JSON escapes. 364 or earlier sap:sapstartsrv source_location reads file names that contain a dot and skips the [Thr N] thread marker. 364 or earlier squid:cache, squid:store New sourcetype stanzas for the Data TA’s new Squid routes, with no automatic key=value fields. 363 or earlier linux:sudolog command holds the whole command, with continuation lines joined and escapes removed. 363 or earlier lastlog USERNAME accepts user names with -, the header line is skipped, and the new PORT field holds lastlog’s Port column (for example <console>). 363 or earlier sap:hana:audit status and target_user are read for every action, not only connect-type actions; user and privilege statements match in any letter case and when quoted; audit_datetime is set on records whose time ends in Z. 363 or earlier squid:access Proxy fields are also extracted from Squid’s logformat=splunk_recommended_squid form. 363 or earlier sap:abap:gateway, sap:scc:http_access, sap:sapstartsrv, sap:saphostexec gw_error_detail, the Cloud Connector’s http_version and the error_message of the Start Service and the Host Agent end where the line ends.

docs.title: Data TA
docs.text:
The Data TA does its work where LogServ data is parsed, on the heavy forwarders or a single instance, so its changes reach events parsed after it is updated there; events indexed earlier keep their sourcetype and fields. Apply every row whose build is later than yours. Coming from 0.0.5, 0.0.6 or 0.1.1, every 0.1.2 row applies: their routing is that of the first 0.1.2 build.

Coming from Data TA Changed in What changes, and what to do A build before 1792598960 1792598960 (2026-10-21) Parsing, routing and filtering are unchanged, and nothing has to be saved again. The AWS S3 Direct screen accepts the Splunk Add-on for AWS 8.1.0 and any later version (earlier builds warned about any version but 8.1.0) and no longer blocks a search head or Splunk Cloud. A build before 1792189743 1792189743 (2026-10-16) Before you update, remove routes of your own from the Data TA’s local/transforms.conf, such as the six (?s)^ routes of build 1791935359 if you added them there as a test (Version Check): local/ wins over default/ key by key, so the old REGEX would stay in effect with the new 100,000-character window, a combination that exceeds Splunk’s regex match limit. Every metadata rule and sourcetype route now reads up to 100,000 characters of a line; earlier builds read 4,096. An AWS event longer than about 4 KB used to keep the input’s own host and source, get no folder fields and stay sap_logserv_logs, while the filters (from 1791565776) already judged it by its folder fields; it now gets its real host, source, folder fields and sourcetype. Searches of your own that find such events under sap_logserv_logs need their final sourcetype. The ICM route takes only the ABAP ICM folder (abap/icm): a webdispatcher/icm folder keeps sap_logserv_logs. The BIND, Windows and sssd routes match only within the source value. A build before 1791935359 1791935359 (2026-10-13) Data TA builds from 0.0.4.1 up to, but not including, this one carry five or six routes whose cost grows with the square of the line length: 2.4 ms of CPU per event on the lab heavy forwarder, about 400 events a second for one pipeline set. Update every instance that parses LogServ data before you size or add hardware (Capacity Planning and First Start). A build before 1791565776 1791565776 (2026-10-09) Configuration → Filters gains Include Sources and Exclude Sources (empty by default), and the filter rules read the whole line. Behaviour change: an Include Filters list that mixes */* or a standalone * with other entries now keeps every event. Before, */*, linux/cron dropped every event without folder fields, and *, linux/cron kept only linux/cron. To keep an allow-list, remove */* and * from it. HANA .trc files and backup.log delivered without folder fields get sap:hana:tracelogs from their path (Data Delivered Without Folder Fields). With Filtering on, open Configuration → Filters after the update, click Save, and on a Deployment Server click Deploy to Forwarders, so the forwarders get the regenerated rules. On a Deployment Server with Filtering on and Days in the Past above 0, the daily filter refresh now finds and reloads the server class (before, whether it found it depended on the default app of the user the refresh runs as, and when it did not, the forwarders kept the previous cutoff), so each forwarder in the server class restarts about once a day to apply the new cutoff (Days in the Past). Use App build 377 or later with it: the Data Doctor of App build 376 and earlier ignores source rules and reports folder patterns with * or ? as only partly read (Reading the Active Filter Configuration). A build before 1790374045 1790374045 (2026-09-25) The Data TA declares the folder paths linux/proxy and linux/pacemaker: with Filtering on and an explicit Include Filters list, add them where those logs should be kept, because events under them are dropped at the forwarder (Upgrade Notifications). A build before 1790368041 1790368041 (2026-09-25) Squid’s cache.log goes to squid:cache and store.log to squid:store; access.log stays squid:access, and all three keep the proxy/squid filter path. Events indexed earlier keep squid:access. The App’s dashboards count access.log lines only; searches of your own that read the other two files under squid:access need the new names. A build before 1790292318 1790292318 (2026-09-24) Long NDJSON lines are unwrapped and kept whole: lines with many escaped characters, from about 1.5 KB, no longer keep their envelope, and lines up to 100,000 bytes are no longer cut at 10,000. Events indexed earlier keep their envelope. A 0.0.5 build whose version reads 0.0.5.0 (four parts), or 0.0.5.1 0.0.5 (version 0.0.5) The audit index is logserv_ai_assistant_audit; those builds define _ai_assistant_audit instead. Where the Data TA holds your index definitions, the update defines the new index; where they are defined elsewhere (the indexer tier, Splunk Cloud), create logserv_ai_assistant_audit there (Create the Indexes), and update a copy of the Data TA that an indexer holds. Then check that Audit index name under Settings → AI Assistant → General → Audit & Telemetry reads logserv_ai_assistant_audit. Audit events written earlier stay in _ai_assistant_audit and are not searchable under the new name. 0.0.4.2 or earlier 0.0.5 The cron, warn, sudo and slapd logs move from Splunk’s syslog sourcetype to linux:cron, linux:warn, linux:sudolog and linux:slapd. Events indexed as syslog keep it until retention removes them; the App’s Linux and Change & Configuration searches read both.

Splunk Add-on for AWS. Nothing in the solution enforces a version. Splunk’s advisory SVD-2026-1005 (third-party package fixes) says to upgrade the add-on to 8.2.2 or later, so run 8.2.2 or later on the forwarders; these docs were checked with 8.3.1. The AWS S3 Direct screen was validated with 8.1.0 and shows an advisory for an older version.

AWS Copy stacks. A stack created from an earlier splunk-logserv-remote-s3-copy.yaml runs its Lambda on python3.9, which AWS has deprecated. The current template uses python3.12; the function’s code is unchanged. Update the stack with the current template, keeping your parameter values (AWS Remote S3 Copy guide). Filter stacks already run python3.12 and need no change.

Cloud Provider dropdown. If the Data TA’s Configuration → Cloud Provider tab is set to a cloud on your forwarders, read Choose Cloud Attribution before you change anything. The inputs of the LogServ Azure and GCP add-ons always stamp cloud_provider, the AWS S3 Direct screen stamps every input it creates, and the dropdown adds its value beside such a stamp, not in its place, so those events carry the field twice. The recommended setting is Not set, with _meta = cloud_provider::aws on each SQS-Based S3 input; to move a fleet from the dropdown set to AWS to that setting, see Alternative for AWS-Only Fleets. A change applies to events parsed after it.

docs.title: LogServ Azure and GCP Add-ons
docs.text:
• Update them on each heavy forwarder, or search head, that runs them, never through the Deployment Server: each input’s credential (the Azure SAS, the GCP service-account key) is stored, encrypted, in the add-on’s own local/passwords.conf on that instance. An app upgrade keeps that file, and nothing has to be moved to system/local; a Deployment Server push would replace it. See Install the Azure Add-on and the GCP Setup Guide.
  • Any 0.1.2 build runs the same code. Builds 1792558069 (Azure) and 1792558072 (GCP) change only the workloads the add-ons declare (so that a search head is an allowed target, Splunk Cloud included) and their README and Inputs-page text, and builds 1792213309 and 1792213464 only their third-party notices, package pins and README text; every Python file is that of the first 0.1.2 builds.
  • Azure, coming from 0.0.5. 0.0.5 read Azure data with the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services (Splunkbase 3110), which its setup guide placed in the SAP_LogServ_HeavyForwarders server class. Set up the LogServ Azure add-on on the forwarder that will read SAP’s queue (Configure the Input), then disable the Microsoft Cloud Services input that read the LogServ storage, so no blob is indexed twice.
  • GCP, onboarded with an SAP-issued key. The add-on signs in with the service-account key its input holds, wherever that account lives, so a deployment that uses a key SAP issued for a service account in the SAP-managed LogServ project needs no change. New onboarding uses the customer-homed sequence in The Onboarding Sequence.
  • GCP, coming from the Splunk Add-on for Google Cloud Platform (Splunkbase 3088). As of its version 5.0.3 (checked 2026-07-05), its Cloud Pub/Sub Based Bucket input does not decompress gzipped objects, so it fails on LogServ’s *.json.gz objects, and it needs roles/pubsub.viewer beyond the roles SAP documents. Use the LogServ GCP add-on, and disable any 3088 input on the LogServ subscription.

docs.title: 3. Upgrade Sequence
docs.text:
The packages can be updated in either order. This order checks the forwarders before the App and leaves the Dashboard Data rebuild, which reads the indexed events, for the end.

  1. Prepare.
    • Find your builds and note the work-list rows that apply.
    • Export the threat-intel lists you keep by hand. logserv_ti_malicious_domains.csv, logserv_ti_malicious_ips.csv and logserv_ti_compromised_credentials.csv ship in the App’s lookups/ directory as header-only files, so an upgrade may replace rows you added. For example | inputlookup logserv_ti_malicious_domains | outputcsv logserv_ti_malicious_domains_backup writes to $SPLUNK_HOME/var/run/splunk/csv/ on the search head; re-upload the list afterwards under Settings → Lookups → Lookup table files. A list that a recurring saved search writes (Threat Intelligence Integration) is refilled on that search’s next run.
    • Note the local/ overrides the rows name: search overrides in local/savedsearches.conf, [collections/...] stanzas in the App’s metadata/local.meta, optInVersion lines in local/ai_assistant_acks.conf, and routes of your own in the Data TA’s local/transforms.conf. Remove those routes before you update the Data TA.
    • Plan the Dashboard Data rebuild for a time clear of the nightly retention window: 00:34–00:58, 01:30–01:58 and 02:34–02:36 in the search head’s local time.
  2. Update the Data TA where it parses data, as described in Updating the Data TA below.
  3. Update the LogServ Azure and GCP add-ons on each heavy forwarder, or search head, that runs them: Apps → Manage Apps → Install app from file with Upgrade app selected, or $SPLUNK_HOME/bin/splunk install app <tarball> -update 1, then restart Splunk. On a Splunk Cloud search head, update them as private apps (On Splunk Cloud).
  4. Check each forwarder’s build (Version Check).
  5. Update the LogServ App on the search head. On Splunk Enterprise: Apps → Manage Apps → Install app from file, select the tarball and Upgrade app, then restart Splunk when asked. On a search head cluster, never update the members one by one: on the deployer, replace $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/shcluster/apps/splunk_app_sap_logserv with the new build, keeping any local/ you keep there, then run splunk apply shcluster-bundle (Splunk Enterprise: search head cluster). On Splunk Cloud, see On Splunk Cloud.
  6. Hard-refresh the browser, then open About and check that it shows build 394.
  7. Work through the App rows of the work list, the Dashboard Data rebuild included (How to Rebuild a Row). If you also load history from S3 with the AWS S3 Direct screen, let that backfill finish first, so that one rebuild includes it.
  8. Enterprise Security content. The App ships its splunk_sap_logserv_es_* searches enabled: correlation searches hourly, behavioral anomalies daily, feeds every 4 hours.
