docs.title: Third-Party Software Licenses
docs.text: Splunk for SAP LogServ bundles third-party software. The LogServ App, a webpack-built React single-page application, bundles open-source npm packages and three font families, and it includes search-time parsing content taken from two archived Splunk add-ons. The Data TA and the Azure and GCP ingest add-ons bundle nine open-source Python packages, and their configuration pages, generated by Splunk’s UCC framework, carry UCC’s prebuilt React bundle. Each component carries its own license, and per those licenses we preserve attribution and ship the full license text with each package.

docs.title: Where to find the full notices
docs.text:
The list of third-party npm packages in the App’s build tree — names, versions, declared licenses, and full license text — is delivered in two places:

  • Inside the App tarball — splunk_app_sap_logserv/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md (the file is at the root of the installed app directory after extraction)
  • At the source-tree root — the same file lives at the root of the GitHub release source tarball

Each add-on ships its own THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md for its Python packages; see Python packages in the add-ons.

The App’s file is generated at build time from the build workspace’s resolved node_modules/ tree. It lists every package at the top level of that tree, at the version installed there: the libraries bundled into the App’s JavaScript, and also the build, lint, type-check and test tools used to produce it (webpack, TypeScript, Babel, ESLint, Stylelint, Prettier, Jest and their dependencies), which are not shipped. The list is a deliberate superset for attribution. About 300 of the packages are reachable from the App’s runtime dependencies, and webpack bundles only the code the App imports.

A copy of a package that the tree holds nested inside another package, at a different version, is not listed separately. In the v0.1.2 build tree, 32 such copies are reachable from the App’s runtime dependencies, for example d3-scale 4.0.2 under @splunk/visualization-canvas, beside the listed d3-scale 3.3.0. Each of them is under the MIT, ISC or BSD-3-Clause license, but not always under the license of the version that is listed: several d3-* packages are BSD-3-Clause in the listed version and ISC in the nested one, or the other way round.

The file’s sections on the absorbed Splunk add-ons and the bundled fonts are fixed text that the build writes each time.

docs.title: License-distribution summary (v0.1.2)
docs.text:
The v0.1.2 notices list 1236 unique top-level packages from the build tree, runtime libraries and build and test tooling together (see the Summary block at the top of the shipped THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md for the authoritative figures). The license breakdown of the listed packages:

License (SPDX as declared) Count Inclusion obligation MIT 1012 Copyright + license text (preserved in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md) ISC 64 Copyright + license text Apache-2.0 57 License text + NOTICE if present BSD-3-Clause 46 Copyright + license text BSD-2-Clause 22 Copyright + license text SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE.md (11 of the 27 @splunk/* libraries) 11 Covered as a Splunk Extension under §1.C of Splunk General Terms BlueOak-1.0.0 4 License text CC0-1.0 / 0BSD / MIT-0 7 Public-domain or near-public-domain (no obligation) BSD-3-Clause AND Apache-2.0 1 License text MIT AND Zlib 1 License text MIT OR Apache-2.0 1 Either license; we attribute MIT MIT OR CC0-1.0 1 Either license; we attribute MIT MPL-2.0 OR Apache-2.0 1 We do not modify the file; either license is satisfied MIT OR SEE LICENSE IN FEEL-FREE.md 1 MIT chosen MPL-2.0 (axe-core) 1 License text only (we do not modify the source) EPL-2.0 (elkjs) 1 License text only — file-level weak copyleft; we bundle the package unmodified Python-2.0 1 License text CC-BY-4.0 / CC-BY-3.0 2 Attribution preserved (no declared license field) 2 See note below

Some rows come only from build, lint and test tooling and are not in the shipped JavaScript: MPL-2.0 (axe-core), Python-2.0 (argparse), CC-BY-4.0 (caniuse-lite), CC-BY-3.0 (spdx-exceptions), the four BlueOak-1.0.0 packages, the two MIT-0 packages (@csstools/*) and MIT OR CC0-1.0 (type-fest).

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• No GPL/AGPL/LGPL components are included in the App’s npm dependency tree. The npm license posture is fully compatible with commercial redistribution under the standard Splunkbase model.
  • One file-level weak-copyleft component is bundled: elkjs (EPL-2.0, the Environment Topology layout engine), unmodified. EPL-2.0 is file-scoped copyleft (not project-scoped like GPL), and its obligations are satisfied by preserving the license text and not modifying the source, which we do. It is not in the GPL/AGPL/LGPL family. (In the 0.1.x line, the elkjs entry joined the generated notices in App build 333, when the package’s formal dependency declaration was added.) axe-core (MPL-2.0) is in the build tree only as a dependency of the eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y lint plugin and is not in the shipped JavaScript.
  • Two packages without a declared license field — @mapbox/jsonlint-lines-primitives@2.0.2 and uuid-v4@0.1.0 — are present as transitive dependencies. Both are de-facto open-source and have been on the public npm registry for years; reviewers preparing legal attestations should consult the upstream repositories listed in the per-component entries of THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md for any final disposition.
  • @splunk/* packages (27 in total). Eleven declare SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE.md: the @splunk/visualization* family, @splunk/charting-bundle and @splunk/async-dynamic-options-evaluator. They are covered as a Splunk Extension under §1.C of the Splunk General Terms, the standard mechanism for redistributing Splunk UI libraries inside a Splunkbase-distributed app. The other 16, such as @splunk/react-ui, @splunk/themes and @splunk/splunk-utils, declare Apache-2.0 and are counted in the Apache-2.0 row above.

docs.title: Bundled fonts
docs.text: Beyond npm packages, the App bundles three font families (listed in the shipped notices file’s “Bundled fonts” section): Inter (SIL Open Font License 1.1), Roboto Mono (Apache-2.0), and Sharp Sans (a commercial typeface used under Cisco’s license — not open source; do not extract or reuse it outside this App).

docs.title: Absorbed Splunk add-ons
docs.text:
The App includes search-time parsing content — props.conf, transforms.conf, eventtypes.conf and tags.conf entries, and lookup files — taken from two archived add-ons published by Splunk Inc. This content is under Splunk licenses, not open-source licenses; the license texts ship in the App’s LICENSES/ folder, and the shipped notices file’s “Absorbed Splunk add-ons” section describes it.

Add-on License Sourcetypes Lookups Splunk Add-on for ISC BIND v2.0.0 (Splunk_TA_isc-bind) LicenseRef-Splunk-1-2020 (LICENSES/LicenseRef-Splunk-1-2020.txt) isc:bind:query, isc:bind:queryerror, isc:bind:lameserver, isc:bind:network, isc:bind:transfer isc_bind_action, isc_bind_category, isc_bind_reply_code, isc_bind_severities Splunk Add-on for Squid Proxy v2.1.0 (Splunk_TA_squid) LicenseRef-Splunk-8-2021 (LICENSES/LicenseRef-Splunk-8-2021.txt) squid:access (squid:access:recommended was not absorbed) squid_actions_210, squid_httpstatus

One lookup differs from the original add-on: squid_actions_210.csv maps TCP_DENIED, UDP_DENIED, TCP_SWAPFAIL and UDP_INVALID to action=denied, where the original uses the CIM-standard blocked, because the App’s proxy panels read denied. See Proxy Analytics.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: The sections above cover the LogServ App’s npm dependencies, its bundled fonts and the absorbed Splunk add-on content. The add-ons’ Python packages and the notices of their UCC configuration pages follow.

docs.title: Python packages in the add-ons
docs.text:
The Data TA and the Azure and GCP ingest add-ons bundle the same nine Python packages, at the same versions, in their lib/ folder; Splunk’s UCC build framework installs them. Each package’s own license file ships beside it, in lib/<package>-<version>.dist-info/.

Package Version License (SPDX) defusedxml 0.7.1 PSF-2.0 deprecation 2.1.0 Apache-2.0 packaging 26.3 Apache-2.0 OR BSD-2-Clause PySocks 1.7.1 BSD-3-Clause solnlib 7.0.0 Apache-2.0 sortedcontainers 2.4.0 Apache-2.0 splunk-sdk 2.1.1 Apache-2.0 (the package ships no license file; the notices file below carries the text) splunktaucclib 8.2.0 Apache-2.0 urllib3 1.26.20 MIT
  • requests and splunk are not bundled. The packages above import them from the Splunk platform’s own Python at run time.
  • The add-ons’ notices files. Each add-on ships THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md at its root, naming these packages, the vendored files inside them (two copies of six, urllib3’s backports) and the Apache License 2.0 text, and its lib/requirements.txt pins each package’s exact version with its PyPI file hashes, so a rebuild cannot pick up a newer release unseen: the Data TA since build 1792189743, and the Azure and GCP add-ons since builds 1792213309 and 1792213464.
  • The add-ons’ configuration pages are compiled by UCC and carry their own notice file for the npm packages they contain: appserver/static/js/build/licenses.txt in each add-on.

docs.title: Known advisories: urllib3 1.26.20
docs.text:
The Data TA and the Azure and GCP ingest add-ons bundle urllib3 1.26.20, which vulnerability scanners report as affected by seven advisories: CVE-2025-50181, CVE-2025-66418, CVE-2025-66471, CVE-2026-21441, CVE-2026-44431, CVE-2026-97687 and CVE-2026-97689. We analysed each against the add-ons’ code, and none affects them as shipped:

  • No add-on code uses urllib3. It is loaded only by Splunk’s solutions library (solnlib), whose REST client talks to the local splunkd management port (by default 127.0.0.1:8089) with the add-on’s own session key. The add-ons’ outbound connections (Azure Storage and the Google Cloud APIs) use Python’s standard library, and no script in the Data, Azure or GCP add-ons imports requests or urllib3, directly or through splunk_aoblib.
  • Three need code paths that are never taken - urllib3’s redirect handling with retries turned off, following redirects while streaming a response, and passing credentials on across redirects through a proxy: CVE-2025-50181, CVE-2026-21441 and CVE-2026-44431.
  • Three need a malicious server on the splunkd management port - decompression and chunked-response attacks: CVE-2025-66418, CVE-2025-66471 and CVE-2026-97689. With the default mgmtHostPort that is the loopback interface, so an attacker would already need access to the host; if you bind the management port to a network address, the protection rests on that network.
  • One needs an HTTPS proxy in splunkd’s environment - CVE-2026-97687. If splunkd’s environment sets HTTPS_PROXY, also set NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost (see Installing the Data TA).

Why the add-ons do not ship urllib3 2.x. urllib3 2.x requires OpenSSL 1.1.1 or later, and the Python in Splunk Enterprise 9.4.3 is built with OpenSSL 1.0.2 (OpenSSL 1.0.2zl-fips on our test systems), so urllib3 2.x cannot load there. The releases that fix the newest advisories also require Python 3.10 or later, while Splunk 9.4 runs Python 3.9, and the current splunktaucclib release requires urllib3<2. Splunk Enterprise 9.4.3’s own Python includes urllib3 1.26.19. We expect to stop bundling urllib3, or to move to a 2.x release, when the add-ons’ minimum supported Splunk version moves past 9.4.

docs.title: Refresh policy
docs.text: The App’s THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md is regenerated from the resolved node_modules/ tree at every release. v0.0.5.0 used a one-off generation pass; v0.0.6 and every later release (including v0.1.1 and v0.1.2) refresh the file as part of the standard yarn build pipeline (bin/generate-third-party-notices.js, run after the webpack output lands in stage/), so every package at the top level of the build tree, bundled or not, appears in the notices at the version installed there; nested copies at other versions are not listed separately (see Where to find the full notices). One package was missed this way in earlier builds: elkjs, the Environment Topology layout engine, has no entry in the notices of v0.0.6 builds 252–266, or of the v0.1.1 builds before 333 that bundle it, because it was not declared as a dependency (Release Notes: 0.0.6, build 333). The add-ons’ notices files are maintained by hand, beside their pinned lib/requirements.txt.
